title.en: Volume 445 Biographies 204: Literature 7 -Chen Yuyi, Wang Zao, Ye Mengde, Cheng Ju, Zhang Nie, Han Ju, Zhu Dunru, Ge Shengzhong, Xiong Ke, Zhaofan of Zhangji
title.raw: 卷四百四十五 列傳第二百〇四 文苑七 陳與義 汪藻 葉夢得 程俱 張嵲 韓駒 朱敦儒 葛勝仲 熊克 張即之趙蕃 Volume 445 Biographies 204: Literature 7 -Chen Yuyi, Wang Zao, Ye Mengde, Cheng Ju, Zhang Nie, Han Ju, Zhu Dunru, Ge Shengzhong, Xiong Ke, Zhaofan of Zhangji

sentences.zh: 文苑七

translations.literal: Literature Garden, Part Seven.
translations.idiomatic: Literature, Part Seven.

sentences.zh: ○陳與義汪藻葉夢得程俱張嵲韓駒朱敦儒葛勝仲熊克張即之

translations.literal: Chen Yuyi, Wang Zao, Ye Mengde, Cheng Ju, Zhang Wei, Han Ju, Zhu Dunru, Ge Shengzhong, Xiong Ke, and Zhang Jizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuyi, Wang Zao, Ye Mengde, Cheng Ju, Zhang Wei, Han Ju, Zhu Dunru, Ge Shengzhong, Xiong Ke, and Zhang Jizhi.

sentences.zh: 〈（趙蕃附）〉

translations.literal: (with Zhao Fan appended)
translations.idiomatic: (with Zhao Fan appended)

sentences.zh: 陳與義

translations.literal: Chen Yuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuyi

sentences.zh: 陳與義，字去非，其先居京兆，自曾祖希亮始遷洛。

translations.literal: Chen Yuyi, styled Qufei. His forebears had dwelt in Jingzhao; from his great-grandfather Xiliang onward they moved to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuyi, whose style name was Qufei, came of a family originally from Jingzhao. His great-grandfather Xiliang was the first to settle in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 故為洛人。

translations.literal: Therefore he was a man of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was thus reckoned a native of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 與義天資卓偉，為兒時已能作文，致名譽，流輩斂衽，莫敢與抗。

translations.literal: Yuyi's natural endowment was outstanding and lofty. Even as a child he could compose essays and win renown; his peers drew in their sleeves and none dared contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyi possessed a towering natural talent. As a boy he already wrote with distinction and won a reputation; his contemporaries held back and none dared measure themselves against him.

sentences.zh: 登政和三年上舍甲科，授開德府教授。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe he passed the top grade of the Upper College examination and was appointed professor at Kaide Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1113 he took first place in the Upper College examination and was made professor at Kaide Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累遷太學博士，擢符寶郎，尋謫監陳留酒稅。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Erudite of the Imperial Academy, then selected as Gentleman of the Talismans and Seals, and soon demoted to supervisor of the wine tax at Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Erudite of the Imperial Academy and then Gentleman of the Talismans and Seals, but was soon demoted to overseer of the wine tax at Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 及金人入汴，高宗南遷，遂避亂襄漢，轉湖湘，逾嶺嶠。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens entered Bianjing and Emperor Gaozong moved south, he thereupon fled the turmoil through Xiang and Han, turned to Hunan and the lakes, and crossed the mountain ranges of the far south.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens took Bianjing and Gaozong withdrew to the south, he fled the chaos through the middle Yangtze, wandered Hunan and the lake country, and crossed the southern ranges.

sentences.zh: 久之，召為兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: After a long while he was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled and appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年夏，至行在。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Shaoxing he reached the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 1131 he arrived at the court in exile.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人，兼掌內制。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and concurrently directed inner-court compositions.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and put in charge of imperial drafting.

sentences.zh: 拜吏部侍郎，尋以徽猷閣直學士 知湖州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel; soon afterward, as Academician Expositor of the Huixuan Pavilion, he governed Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of Personnel, then shortly afterward served as prefect of Huzhou with the title Academician Expositor of the Huixuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 召為給事中。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the post of Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 駁議詳雅。

translations.literal: His rebuttals and memorials were detailed and refined.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials of objection were learned and elegant.

sentences.zh: 又以顯謨閣直學士提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: He was again made Academician Expositor of the Xianmo Pavilion and put in charge of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again named Academician Expositor of the Xianmo Pavilion and appointed superintendent of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 被召，會宰相有不樂與義者，復用為中書舍人、直學士院。

translations.literal: When he was summoned back, it happened that a chief minister disliked Yuyi, and he was again employed as Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and member of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: On his recall a chief minister who disliked him intervened, and he was reappointed Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 六年九月，高宗如平江，十一月， 拜翰林學士、知制誥。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year Emperor Gaozong went to Pingjiang; in the eleventh month Yuyi was appointed Hanlin Academician and Drafter of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of 1136 the emperor traveled to Pingjiang; in the eleventh month Yuyi was made Hanlin Academician and Drafter of Edicts.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，參知政事，唯師用道德以輔朝廷，務尊主威而振綱紀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year he became Vice Grand Councilor, instructing only by moral teaching to assist the court and striving to honor the sovereign's authority and revive discipline and law.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1137 he was made Vice Grand Councilor. He sought to guide the court through moral example alone and to restore the emperor's authority and the discipline of government.

sentences.zh: 時丞相趙鼎言：“人多謂中原有可圖之勢，宜便進兵，恐他時 咎今日之失機。”

translations.literal: At that time Chief Councilor Zhao Ding said: "Many people say the Central Plain presents a situation that can be seized; we ought to advance the army at once, lest later they blame us for missing today's opportunity."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chief Councilor Zhao Ding said, "Many argue that the north can still be recovered and that we should march immediately, lest posterity blame us for letting this moment slip."

sentences.zh: 上曰：“今梓宮與太后、淵聖皆未還，若不與金議和，則無可還之理。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "At present the imperial coffin, the empress dowager, and the former emperor Qinsheng have not yet returned. If we do not negotiate peace with the Jin, there is no principle by which they can be brought back."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The late emperor's coffin, the empress dowager, and the captive former emperor have not yet been returned. Unless we treat with the Jin, there is no way to secure their release."

sentences.zh: 與義曰：“若和議成，豈不賢於用兵，萬一無成，則用兵必不免。”

translations.literal: Yuyi said: "If the peace talks succeed, would that not be better than resorting to arms? If by any chance they fail, then war cannot be avoided."
translations.idiomatic: Yuyi said, "If peace succeeds, is that not preferable to war? And if it fails, war will become unavoidable in any case."

sentences.zh: 上 曰：“然。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is so."

sentences.zh: 三月，從帝如建康。

translations.literal: In the third month he followed the emperor to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he accompanied the emperor to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 明年，扈蹕還臨安。

translations.literal: The next year he escorted the imperial procession back to Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he escorted the court back to Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 以疾請，復以資政殿學士知湖州，陛辭，帝勞問甚渥，遂請閑，提舉臨安洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and resigned; he was again made Academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Huzhou. At his audience of leave the emperor comforted and questioned him with great kindness; he then requested retirement and was put in charge of the Dongxiao Abbey in Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and stepped down, then served again as prefect of Huzhou with the title Academician of the Zizheng Hall. At his farewell audience the emperor treated him with exceptional warmth; he then asked to retire and was made superintendent of the Dongxiao Abbey near Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 十一月，卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh month, at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 與義容狀儼恪，不妄言笑，平居雖謙以接物，然內剛不可犯。

translations.literal: Yuyi's bearing was solemn and respectful; he did not speak or laugh rashly. In ordinary life, though he received others with humility, inwardly he was firm and not to be transgressed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyi was grave in manner and sparing of speech and laughter. Though courteous in daily dealings, he was inwardly unyielding and not to be crossed.

sentences.zh: 其薦士於朝，退未嚐以語人，士以是多之。

translations.literal: When he recommended scholars to the court, after retiring he never spoke of it to others; scholars for this reason greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: When he recommended men to office he never mentioned it afterward, and scholars admired him all the more for that discretion.

sentences.zh: 尤長於詩，體物寓興，清邃紆餘，高舉橫厲，上下陶、謝、韋、柳之間。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in poetry: embodying things and lodging inspiration, clear and deep, winding and ample, soaring high and sweeping boldly—ranging between Tao, Xie, Wei, and Liu.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled above all in poetry, giving voice to things observed and feelings stirred—clear, deep, and lingering, yet also bold and soaring—standing with Tao Yuanming, Xie Lingyun, Wei Yingwu, and Liu Zongyuan.

sentences.zh: 嘗賦墨梅，徽宗嘉賞之，以是受知於上云。

translations.literal: He once composed a poem on ink plum blossoms; Emperor Huizong praised it, and by this he won the sovereign's notice.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a poem on ink-painted plum blossoms that Huizong admired, and through it he came to the emperor's attention.

sentences.zh: 汪藻，字彥章，饒州德興人。

translations.literal: Wang Zao, styled Yanzhang, was a native of Dexing in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zao, whose style name was Yanzhang, came from Dexing in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 幼穎異，入太學，中進士第。

translations.literal: As a youth he was unusually bright; he entered the Imperial Academy and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was precocious as a boy, entered the Imperial Academy, and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 調婺州觀察推官，改宣州教授，稍遷江西提舉學事司幹當公事。

translations.literal: He was assigned as investigating censor at Wuzhou, changed to professor at Xuanzhou, and was gradually promoted to clerk for general affairs in the Jiangxi Education Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as investigating censor at Wuzhou, then made professor at Xuanzhou, and later rose to a clerkship in the Jiangxi Education Commission.

sentences.zh: 徽宗親製《君臣慶會閣詩》，群臣皆賡進，惟藻和篇，眾莫能及。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong personally composed the "Poem of the Monarch and Ministers' Celebratory Assembly Hall"; all the ministers submitted matching verses, but only Zao's response could not be matched by the rest.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong wrote the "Poem of the Monarch and Ministers' Celebratory Assembly Hall," the whole court submitted matching verses, yet none could rival Zao's response.

sentences.zh: 時胡伸亦以文名，人為之語曰：“江左二寶，胡伸、汪藻。”

translations.literal: At that time Hu Shen was also famed for literature; people made a saying of it: "The two treasures of the lands south of the Yangtze—Hu Shen and Wang Zao."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shen was then equally renowned for letters, and people said, "The two treasures of the south—Hu Shen and Wang Zao."

sentences.zh: 尋除《九域圖志》所編修官，再遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed to compiler of the Nine Regions Gazetteer Office, and was again transferred to Assistant Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed compiler for the Nine Regions Gazetteer project and later promoted to Assistant Compiler.

sentences.zh: 時王黼與藻同舍，素不鹹，出通判宣州，提點江州太平觀，投閑凡八年，終黼之世不得用。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Fu had been Zao's roommate; they had never been on good terms. Zao was sent out as vice prefect of Xuanzhou and superintendent of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou; he lived in retirement for eight years in all and to the end of Fu's lifetime was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu had once been his roommate and they had never gotten along. Zao was sent out as vice prefect of Xuanzhou and then superintendent of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou, where he spent eight idle years and was never employed again while Fu lived.

sentences.zh: 欽宗即位，召為屯田員外郎，再遷太常少卿、起居舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong ascended the throne, Zao was summoned as Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture; he was again transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and Recorder of the Emperor's Actions.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzong came to the throne Zao was recalled as Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, then promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and Recorder of the Emperor's Actions.

sentences.zh: 高宗踐祚，召試中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Zao was summoned and examined for the post of Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended the throne Zao was examined and appointed Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時次揚州，藻多論奏，宰相黃潛善惡之，遂假他事，免為集英殿修撰、提舉太 平觀。

translations.literal: At that time the court was temporarily at Yangzhou; Zao submitted many memorials of discussion. Chief Councilor Huang Qianshan disliked him and, on a pretext of another matter, dismissed him to Compiler of the Jiying Hall and superintendent of the Taiping Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was at Yangzhou Zao submitted many policy memorials. Chief Councilor Huang Qianshan took offense and, on a pretext, removed him to Compiler of the Jiying Hall and superintendent of the Taiping Abbey.

sentences.zh: 明年，復召為中書舍人兼直學士院，擢給事中，遷兵部待郎兼侍講，拜翰林學士。

translations.literal: The next year he was again summoned as Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and concurrently attached to the Hanlin Academy, promoted to Supervising Censor, transferred to Vice Minister of War and Lecturer-in-Waiting, and appointed Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled as Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and to the Hanlin Academy, promoted to Supervising Censor, then Vice Minister of War and Lecturer-in-Waiting, and finally Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 帝以所禦白團扇，親書“紫誥仍兼綰，黃麻似《六經》”十字以賜，縉紳豔 之。

translations.literal: The emperor took a white round fan from his own use and personally wrote the ten characters "Purple edicts still bound together; yellow edict paper like the Six Classics" to bestow on him; the gentry admired it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took a white round fan from his own hand and inscribed ten characters—"Purple edicts still bound together; yellow edict paper like the Six Classics"—and gave it to him, to the envy of the court.

sentences.zh: 屬時多事，詔令類出其手。

translations.literal: As the times were full of urgent affairs, edicts and orders mostly came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: In those troubled years most imperial edicts passed through his pen.

sentences.zh: 嚐論諸大將擁重兵，浸成外重之勢，且陳所以待將帥者三事，後十年，卒如其策。

translations.literal: He once argued that the great generals, holding heavy armies, were gradually forming a situation in which the outer regions grew strong; he also set forth three measures for how to treat commanders. Ten years later events at last followed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: He once warned that the great generals, holding vast armies, were tipping the balance of power toward the provinces, and he laid out three principles for handling commanders. A decade later events unfolded exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 又言：“崇、觀以來，貲結權幸，奴 事閹宦，與開邊誤國，得職名自觀文殿大學士而下直秘閣、官至銀青光祿大夫者，近稍鐫褫，而建炎恩宥，又當甄復，盍依國初法，止中大夫。”

translations.literal: He also said: "Since the Chongning and Daguan reigns, those who bought favor with the powerful, served eunuchs like slaves, and joined in frontier campaigns to harm the state—those who obtained posts from Academician of the Guanwen Hall down to Direct Access to the Secret Archives and ranks up to Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal—have recently been somewhat stripped of honors, yet under the Jianyan amnesty they are again to be screened for restoration. Why not follow the law of the dynasty's founding and stop at Grandee of Governance?"
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that since the Chongning and Daguan reigns men who bought influence, fawned on eunuchs, and pushed reckless frontier wars had been rewarded with lofty titles from Academician of the Guanwen Hall down to Direct Access to the Secret Archives and ranks as high as Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal. Though some honors had lately been stripped away, the Jianyan amnesty threatened to restore them. He urged following the founding precedent and capping such men at Grandee of Governance.

sentences.zh: 紹興 元年，除龍圖閣直學士、知湖州，以顏真卿盡忠唐室，嚐守是邦，乞表章之，詔賜廟忠烈。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing he was made Academician Expositor of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Huzhou. Because Yan Zhenqing had been wholly loyal to the Tang house and once governed that region, Zao begged to honor him in a public proclamation; an edict granted his temple the title Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131 he was appointed Academician Expositor of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Huzhou. Citing Yan Zhenqing's loyalty to the Tang and his former service in that prefecture, he asked that Yan be publicly honored; the court granted his temple the posthumous title Loyal and Stern.

sentences.zh: 又言：「古者有國必有史，古書榻前議論之辭，則有時政記，錄柱下見聞 之實，則有起居注，類而次之，謂之日曆，修而成之，謂之實錄。

translations.literal: He also said: "In antiquity, where there was a state there was certainly a history. Discussions before the couch in ancient books were recorded in Current Policy Notes; what was seen and heard below the pillars was recorded in Records of the Emperor's Actions. When these were classified and arranged in order they were called the Calendar; when edited and completed they were called the Veritable Record."
translations.idiomatic: He also observed: "Every state in antiquity had a history. Court deliberations were entered in Current Policy Notes, and what the censors observed below the pillars went into Records of the Emperor's Actions. Arranged in sequence these became the Calendar; polished into final form they became the Veritable Record.

sentences.zh: 今逾三十年，無復日曆，何以示來世？

translations.literal: Now more than thirty years have passed without any Calendar—how can this be shown to later ages?
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty years have now passed without a Calendar. How can we leave posterity nothing to read?

sentences.zh: 乞即臣所領州，許臣訪尋故家文書，纂集元符庚辰以來詔 旨，為日曆之備。」

translations.literal: I beg that in the prefecture I now govern I be permitted to search out documents in old families' collections and compile edicts from the gengchen year of Yuanfu onward as material for the Calendar."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that, within the prefecture I govern, I be allowed to seek out documents from old families and compile edicts from 1098 onward as the foundation for a new Calendar."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 史館既開，修撰綦崇禮言不必別設外局，乃已。

translations.literal: Once the History Office had been opened, Compiler Qi Chongli said there was no need to set up a separate external bureau, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: After the History Office reopened, Compiler Qi Chongli argued that a separate external bureau was unnecessary, and the project was halted.

sentences.zh: 郡人顏經投匭訴其敷糴軍食，遂貶秩停官。

translations.literal: A man of the prefecture, Yan Jing, submitted a complaint box memorial accusing him of distributing grain to provision the army; he was therefore demoted in rank and suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Yan Jing lodged a complaint accusing him of misallocating grain meant for the army, and Zao was demoted and suspended from office.

sentences.zh: 起知撫州，御史張致遠又論之，予祠。

translations.literal: He was raised to govern Fuzhou, but Censor Zhang Zhiyuan again impeached him and he was given a temple stipend.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed prefect of Fuzhou, but Censor Zhang Zhiyuan attacked him again and he was given only a temple stipend.

sentences.zh: 六年， 修撰範衝言：“日曆，國之大典，比詔藻纂修，事復中止，恐遂散逸，宜令就閑復卒前業。”

translations.literal: In the sixth year Compiler Fan Chong said: "The Calendar is a great canon of the state. Recently an edict ordered Zao to compile it, but the work was again halted; I fear it will be scattered and lost. He should be ordered, while at leisure, to finish his former task."
translations.idiomatic: In 1136 Compiler Fan Chong memorialized that the Calendar was a great state document. Zao had been ordered to compile it, but the work had stalled again and might be lost. He urged that Zao be allowed to finish the project in retirement.

sentences.zh: 詔賜史館修撰餐錢，聽辟屬編類。

translations.literal: An edict granted him maintenance funds as History Office compiler and permitted him to recruit assistants to classify and compile.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him a compiler's stipend from the History Office and allowed him to recruit assistants for the compilation.

sentences.zh: 八年，上所修書，自元符庚辰至宣和 乙巳詔旨，凡六百六十五卷。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he presented the book he had compiled: edicts from the gengchen year of Yuanfu to the yisi year of Xuanhe, six hundred sixty-five juan in all.
translations.idiomatic: In 1138 he presented his compilation: edicts from 1098 through 1125, six hundred sixty-five juan in all.

sentences.zh: 藻再進官，其屬鮑延祖、孟處義鹹增秩有差。

translations.literal: Zao was again promoted in office; his subordinates Bao Yanzu and Meng Chuyi all received differing increases in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zao was promoted again, and his assistants Bao Yanzu and Meng Chuyi received rank increases in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 藻升顯謨閣學士，遣使賜茶藥。

translations.literal: Zao was promoted to Academician of the Xianmo Pavilion; envoys were sent to bestow tea and medicines.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician of the Xianmo Pavilion, and the court sent gifts of tea and medicine.

sentences.zh: 尋知徽州，逾年，徙宣州。

translations.literal: Soon he governed Huizhou; after more than a year he was transferred to Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Huizhou and, a year later, transferred to Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 言者論其嚐為蔡京、王黼之 客，奪職居永州，累赦不宥。

translations.literal: Memorialists argued that he had once been a client of Cai Jing and Wang Fu; his office was stripped and he lived in Yongzhou. Repeated amnesties did not pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged that he had once been a client of Cai Jing and Wang Fu. He was stripped of office and sent to Yongzhou, and repeated amnesties did not restore him.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1154.

sentences.zh: 秦檜死，復職，官其二子。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui died, Zao's offices were restored and his two sons were given posts.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui's death his offices were restored and both his sons were given government posts.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，《徽宗實錄》成書，右仆射湯思退言藻嚐纂集詔旨，比修實錄，所取十蓋七八，深有力於斯文。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the Veritable Record of Emperor Huizong was completed. Right Vice Director Tang Situi said that Zao had once compiled edicts and that, compared with compiling the Veritable Record, seven or eight tenths of what was taken came from him—he had deeply strengthened this branch of learning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1158, when the Veritable Record of Huizong was completed, Right Vice Director Tang Situi noted that Zao's earlier compilation of edicts had supplied seven or eight tenths of the source material and had been indispensable to the work.

sentences.zh: 詔贈端明殿學士。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously granted him the title Academician of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 藻通顯三十年，無屋廬以居。

translations.literal: Zao held prominent office for thirty years yet had no house in which to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Though prominent in office for thirty years, Zao never owned a house of his own.

sentences.zh: 博極群書，老不釋卷，尤喜讀《春秋左氏傳》及《西漢書》。

translations.literal: He mastered all books exhaustively and in old age did not put down his scrolls, especially delighting in reading the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and the History of the Former Han.
translations.idiomatic: He read voraciously and never set books aside even in old age, especially favoring the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and the History of the Former Han.

sentences.zh: 工儷語，多著述，所為製詞，人多傳誦。

translations.literal: He was skilled in parallel prose, wrote many works, and the edict-drafting compositions he made were widely transmitted and recited.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in parallel prose, wrote extensively, and his edict drafts were widely copied and recited.

sentences.zh: 子六人，恬、恪、憺、怲、懍、憘。

translations.literal: He had six sons: Tian, Ke, Dan, Bing, Lin, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Tian, Ke, Dan, Bing, Lin, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 葉夢得

translations.literal: Ye Mengde.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Mengde

sentences.zh: 葉夢得，字少蘊，蘇州吳縣人。

translations.literal: Ye Mengde, styled Shaoyun, was a native of Wu County in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Mengde, whose style name was Shaoyun, came from Wu County in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 嗜學蚤成，多識前言往行，談論亹亹不窮。

translations.literal: He loved learning and matured early; he knew much of what former worthies had said and done, and in discussion his enthusiasm never ran dry.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and matured early, knew the words and deeds of past sages, and could discourse without end.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年登進士第，調丹徒尉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaosheng he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as magistrate of Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1097 he passed the jinshi examination and was posted as magistrate of Dantu.

sentences.zh: 徽宗朝，自婺州教授召為議禮武選編修官。

translations.literal: In the Huizong reign, from professor at Wuzhou he was summoned as compiler for Rites Deliberation and Military Selection.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huizong he was recalled from a professorship at Wuzhou to serve as compiler for Rites Deliberation and Military Selection.

sentences.zh: 用蔡京薦，召 對，言：“自古帝王為治，廣狹大小，規模各不同，然必自先治其心者始。

translations.literal: On Cai Jing's recommendation he was summoned for an audience and said: "From antiquity emperors in governing the realm, whether broad or narrow, large or small, each had a different scale and pattern, yet all necessarily began by first governing their own hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Cai Jing, he was summoned to audience and said, "Emperors of old governed realms of every size by different means, yet all began by governing their own hearts first.

sentences.zh: 今國勢有安危，法度有利害，人材有邪正，民情有休戚，四者，治之大也。

translations.literal: Today the state's power has security and danger; laws and institutions have benefit and harm; human talent has the crooked and the straight; the people's feelings have ease and distress—these four are the great matters of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Today the state's situation has safety and danger, laws and institutions have benefit and harm, personnel may be corrupt or upright, and the people's condition may be happy or miserable; these four are the great matters of government.

sentences.zh: 若不先治其 心，或誘之以貨利，或陷之以聲色，則所謂安危、利害、邪正、休戚者，未嚐不顛倒易位，而況求其功乎？”

translations.literal: If one does not first govern the heart, whether tempted by goods and profit or trapped by sound and color, then what are called security and danger, benefit and harm, the crooked and the straight, ease and distress—have they not always been turned upside down and exchanged places? How much less can one seek achievement?"
translations.idiomatic: Unless the ruler first governs his own heart—whether tempted by profit or ensnared by pleasure—security and danger, benefit and harm, the upright and the corrupt, and the people's welfare will all be reversed. How then can he expect real achievement?"

sentences.zh: 上異其言，特遷祠部郎官。

translations.literal: The emperor was struck by his words and specially promoted him to Gentleman of the Directorate of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and specially promoted him to Gentleman of the Directorate of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 大觀初，京再 相，向所立法度已罷者復行，夢得言：“《周官》太宰以八柄詔王馭群臣，所謂廢置賞罰者，王之事也，太宰得以詔王而不得自專。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daguan reign Jing again became chief minister; laws and institutions previously abolished were revived. Mengde said: "In the Offices of Zhou the Grand Steward uses the eight handles to instruct the king in governing the ministers. What are called dismissal, appointment, reward, and punishment are the king's affairs; the Grand Steward may instruct the king but may not act on his own authority."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daguan reign Cai Jing returned to power and revived laws he had earlier abolished. Mengde said, "In the Offices of Zhou the Grand Steward used the eight handles to advise the king in governing his ministers. Appointment, dismissal, reward, and punishment were the king's prerogatives; the steward could counsel the king but not decide on his own.

sentences.zh: 夫事不過可不可二者而已，以為 可而出於陛下，則前日不應廢，以為不可而不出於陛下，則今不可復，今徒以大臣進退為可否，無乃陛下有未了然於中者乎？”

translations.literal: Matters are nothing more than the two alternatives of permissible and impermissible. If deemed permissible and issued from Your Majesty, then what was abolished the other day ought not to have been abolished; if deemed impermissible and not issued from Your Majesty, then what is done now ought not be revived. Now you merely take a chief minister's advancement or withdrawal as the standard of permissibility—might Your Majesty not yet be fully clear in your inner mind?"
translations.idiomatic: Policy is simply a matter of what is right and what is not. If something is right because Your Majesty decrees it, then what was abolished yesterday should never have been abolished; if it is wrong because it does not come from Your Majesty, then it should not be revived today. To let a minister's rise or fall decide what is permissible—is Your Majesty not still unclear in his own mind?"

sentences.zh: 上喜曰：“邇來士多朋比媒進，卿言 獨無觀望。”

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: "Of late scholars mostly form factions and seek advancement through intermediaries; your words alone show no calculation of advantage."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with pleasure, "Lately officials flock together and advance through patronage, but your words show no such calculation."

sentences.zh: 遂除起居郎。

translations.literal: He was thereupon appointed Recorder of the Emperor's Actions.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Recorder of the Emperor's Actions.

sentences.zh: 時用事者喜小有才，夢得言：“自古用人必先辨賢能。

translations.literal: At that time those in power favored men of slight talent. Mengde said: "From antiquity in employing men one must first distinguish the worthy and the capable."
translations.idiomatic: Those in power then favored men of minor talent. Mengde said, "From antiquity, appointing officials began with distinguishing the worthy from the merely capable.

sentences.zh: 賢者，有德之稱，能者，有才之稱，故先王常使德勝才，不使才勝德。

translations.literal: "The worthy" is the name for those with virtue; "the capable" is the name for those with talent. Therefore former kings always made virtue overcome talent and did not let talent overcome virtue.
translations.idiomatic: "Worthy" names those with virtue; "capable" names those with talent. Former kings always let virtue outweigh talent, never the reverse.

sentences.zh: 崇寧以來， 在內惟取議論與朝廷同者為純正，在外惟取推行法今速成者為幹敏，未聞器業任重、識度輕遠者，特有表異。

translations.literal: Since Chongning, within the court only those whose opinions agreed with the court were taken as pure and correct; outside only those who pushed the new laws and achieved quick results were taken as capable and keen. One never heard of those whose capacity and achievement were weighty or whose insight was light yet far-reaching receiving special commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Since Chongning the court had favored only those whose opinions matched its own, and the provinces only those who enforced the new laws with quick results. Men of broad capacity and far-seeing judgment were never singled out for praise.

sentences.zh: 恐用才太勝，願繼今用人以有德為先。”

translations.literal: I fear that employing talent has grown too dominant; I wish that from now on in employing men virtue be put first.
translations.idiomatic: I fear talent has been valued too highly. I ask that hereafter appointments put virtue first."

sentences.zh: 二年，累遷翰林學士，極論士大夫朋黨之弊，專於重內輕外，且乞身先眾人補郡。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted in succession to Hanlin Academician, arguing at length on the harm of faction among scholar-officials and the exclusive emphasis on honoring the inner and slighting the outer, and he begged to take the lead among the multitude in filling a prefectural post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he rose to Hanlin Academician. He spoke at length against faction among officials and the court's habit of favoring capital posts over provincial service, and asked to be the first to take a prefectural appointment.

sentences.zh: 蔡京初欲以童貫宣撫陝西，取青唐。

translations.literal: Cai Jing at first wished to make Tong Guan pacification commissioner of Shaanxi to take Qingtang.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing at first planned to make Tong Guan pacification commissioner of Shaanxi to recover Qingtang.

sentences.zh: 夢得見京問曰：“祖宗時，宣撫使皆是見任執 政，文彥博，韓絳因此即軍中拜相，未有以中人為之。

translations.literal: Mengde saw Jing and asked: "In the time of the ancestral emperors, pacification commissioners were all incumbent chief administrators—Wen Yanbo and Han Jiang were for this reason made chief ministers right in the army. Never has a eunuch been appointed to the post."
translations.idiomatic: Mengde went to Jing and asked, "In the time of our ancestors, Commissioners for Pacification were always sitting chief administrators—Wen Yanbo and Han Jiang were therefore made chief ministers right in camp. No palace intermediary has ever held the post.

sentences.zh: 元豐末，神宗命李憲，雖王珪亦能力爭，此相公所見也。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanfeng Emperor Shenzong appointed Li Xian; even Wang Gui was able to strive against it with all his strength—this is what the chief minister himself witnessed.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanfeng Shenzong appointed Li Xian, and even Wang Gui fought the appointment with all his strength—as you yourself saw, sir.

sentences.zh: 昨八寶恩遽除貫節度使，天下皆知非祖宗法，此已不 可救。

translations.literal: Yesterday, on the Babao grace, Guan was suddenly made military commissioner; all under Heaven know this is not the law of the ancestral emperors—this already cannot be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, on an imperial grace, Guan was suddenly made military commissioner. Everyone knows that violates ancestral precedent, and that mistake cannot be undone.

sentences.zh: 今又付以執政之任，使得青唐，何以處之？”

translations.literal: Now you again entrust him with the duties of chief administrator—if he obtains Qingtang, how will you deal with him?"
translations.idiomatic: Now you would give him the powers of a chief minister as well. If he takes Qingtang, how will you handle him then?"

sentences.zh: 京有慚色，然卒用貫取青唐。

translations.literal: Jing showed a look of shame, yet in the end employed Guan and took Qingtang.
translations.idiomatic: Jing looked ashamed, but in the end he used Guan and Qingtang was taken.

sentences.zh: 三年，以龍圖閣直學士知汝州，尋落職，提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: In the third year, as Academician Expositor of the Longtu Pavilion he governed Ruzhou; soon he lost his post and was put in charge of the Dongxiao Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made prefect of Ruzhou as Academician Expositor of the Longtu Pavilion, but was soon dismissed and appointed superintendent of the Dongxiao Abbey.

sentences.zh: 政和五年，起 知蔡州，復龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenghe he was raised to govern Caizhou and again made Academician Expositor of the Longtu Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In 1115 he was recalled as prefect of Caizhou and restored as Academician Expositor of the Longtu Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 移帥潁昌府，發常平粟振民，常平使者劉寄惡之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command Yingchang Prefecture, issued Ever-Normal Granary grain to relieve the people, and the Ever-Normal Granary commissioner Liu Ji disliked him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to command Yingchang Prefecture, he released Ever-Normal Granary grain to relieve the people, which the granary commissioner Liu Ji resented.

sentences.zh: 宦官楊戩用事，寄括部內，得常平錢五十萬緡，請糴粳米輸後苑以媚戩。

translations.literal: The eunuch Yang Jian held power; Ji levied within the prefecture and obtained five hundred thousand strings of Ever-Normal Granary money, requesting to purchase polished rice to send to the Rear Garden to flatter Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yang Jian was in power. Liu Ji squeezed the prefecture for five hundred thousand strings of Ever-Normal funds and sought to buy polished rice for the imperial gardens to curry favor with Jian.

sentences.zh: 戩委其屬持禦 筆來，責以米樣如蘇州。

translations.literal: Jian sent a subordinate bearing the imperial brush to demand that the rice sample match that of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jian sent an agent with the emperor's brush to demand rice of Suzhou quality.

sentences.zh: 夢得上疏極論潁昌地力與東南異，願隨品色，不報。

translations.literal: Mengde memorialized at length that Yingchang's soil strength differed from the southeast and asked to follow grade and color; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Mengde memorialized that Yingchang's soil could not match the southeast's and asked that grades be adjusted accordingly. His plea went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 時旁郡糾民輸鏹就糴京師，怨聲載道，獨潁昌賴夢得得免。

translations.literal: At that time neighboring prefectures compelled the people to deliver cash to purchase grain for the capital; complaints filled the roads, but Yingchang alone, relying on Mengde, was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring prefectures were forcing people to pay cash to buy grain for the capital, and popular resentment was everywhere. Only Yingchang, thanks to Mengde, was spared.

sentences.zh: 李彥括公田，以黠吏告訐， 籍郟城、舞陽隱田數千頃，民詣府訴者八百戶。

translations.literal: Li Yan surveyed public fields; through a cunning clerk's denunciation he registered several thousand qing of concealed fields in Yancheng and Wuyang; eight hundred households came to the prefecture to complain.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan was surveying public fields. A crafty clerk denounced hidden holdings, and thousands of qing in Yancheng and Wuyang were seized. Eight hundred households petitioned the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 夢得上其事，捕吏按治之，郡人大悅。

translations.literal: Mengde reported the matter upward, arrested the clerk, and investigated him; the people of the prefecture were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Mengde reported the case, arrested the clerk, and prosecuted him, to the great joy of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戩、彥交怒，尋提舉南京鴻慶宮，自是或廢或起。

translations.literal: Jian and Yan were both enraged; soon he was put in charge of the Hongqing Abbey in Nanjing, and from then on was at times dismissed and at times restored.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Yan were furious. Mengde was soon made superintendent of the Hongqing Abbey in Nanjing and thereafter was repeatedly dismissed and recalled.

sentences.zh: 逮高宗駐蹕揚 州，遷翰林學士兼侍讀，除戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong halted at Yangzhou, Mengde was transferred to Hanlin Academician and Lecturer-in-Waiting and made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong halted at Yangzhou, Mengde became Hanlin Academician and Lecturer-in-Waiting and was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 陳“待敵之計有三，曰形、曰勢、曰氣而已。

translations.literal: He stated: "The plans for dealing with the enemy are three: called form, called momentum, and called spirit alone."
translations.idiomatic: He argued: "Strategy against the enemy rests on three things: terrain, material strength, and morale.

sentences.zh: 形以地理山川為本，勢以城池、芻粟、器械為重，氣以將帥士卒為急。

translations.literal: Form takes geography and mountains and rivers as its root; momentum takes walled cities, fodder and grain, and weapons as its weight; spirit takes generals, commanders, and soldiers as its urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Terrain depends on geography; material strength on cities, supplies, and arms; morale on commanders and troops.

sentences.zh: 形固則可 恃以守，勢強則可資以立，氣振則可作以用，如是則敵皆在吾度內矣”。

translations.literal: If form is firm one can rely on it to defend; if momentum is strong one can use it to stand; if spirit is roused one can deploy it for action—thus the enemy is all within our measure."
translations.idiomatic: Firm terrain permits defense, strong resources sustain the state, and high morale makes armies effective—then the enemy lies within our grasp."

sentences.zh: 因請上南巡，阻江為險，以備不虞。

translations.literal: He therefore asked the emperor to tour south, take the river as a barrier for danger, and guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor to move south, use the Yangtze as a defensive barrier, and prepare for contingencies.

sentences.zh: 又請命重臣為宣總使，一居泗上，總兩淮及東方之師以 待敵；

translations.literal: He also asked that a great minister be appointed pacification commissioner-general: one to reside at Si and command the armies of the two Huai regions and the east to await the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed appointing senior ministers as overall commanders—one at Si to gather the Huai and eastern armies against the enemy;

sentences.zh: 一居金陵，總江、浙之路以備退保。

translations.literal: one to reside at Jinling and command the routes of Jiang and Zhe to prepare for withdrawal and defense.
translations.idiomatic: another at Jinling to control the Jiang-Zhe routes as a line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 既而帝駐蹕杭州，遷尚書左丞，奏監司、州縣擅立軍期司掊斂民財者，宜罷。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor halted at Hangzhou; Mengde was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and memorialized that supervisory commissioners and prefectures and counties who on their own established military deadline offices to squeeze the people's wealth should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Hangzhou he was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and urged abolishing the ad hoc military supply offices that prefectures had set up to extort the people.

sentences.zh: 上諭以兵、食二 事最大，當擇大臣分掌。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him that the two matters of troops and provisions were greatest and that great ministers should be chosen to divide their management.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that war and provisions were the greatest concerns and should be entrusted to separate senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎顏岐、知杭州康允之皆嫉夢得，又與宰相朱勝非議論不協，會州民有上書訟夢得過失者，上以夢得深曉財賦，乃除資政殿學士、提 舉中太一宮，專一提領戶部財用，充車駕巡幸頓遞使，辭不拜，歸湖州。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Chancellery Yan Qi and Prefect of Hangzhou Kang Yunzhi both envied Mengde; he also did not agree in discussion with Chief Councilor Zhu Shengfei. It happened that people of the prefecture submitted memorials suing Mengde for faults. The emperor, because Mengde deeply understood finance and taxation, made him Academician of the Zizheng Hall and superintendent of the Zhongtaiyi Abbey, solely to oversee Ministry of Revenue finances and serve as commissioner for the imperial procession's relay supplies; he declined to accept and returned to Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yan Qi and Hangzhou prefect Kang Yunzhi envied him, and he clashed with Chief Councilor Zhu Shengfei. When locals petitioned against him, the emperor—recognizing his mastery of finance—named him Academician of the Zizheng Hall and superintendent of the Zhongtaiyi Abbey with sole charge of revenue for the traveling court. Mengde declined and returned to Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，起為江東安撫大使兼知建康府，兼壽春等六州宣撫使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxing he was raised as Grand Pacification Commissioner of Jiangdong and concurrently prefect of Jiankang, and concurrently pacification commissioner of six prefectures including Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxing era he was recalled as Grand Pacification Commissioner of Jiangdong and prefect of Jiankang, with concurrent authority as pacification commissioner over six prefectures including Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 時建康荒殘， 兵不滿三千。

translations.literal: At that time Jiankang was desolate and ruined; troops numbered fewer than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang lay in ruins, with fewer than three thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 夢得奏移統製官韓世清軍屯建康，崔增屯采石，閻皋分守要害。

translations.literal: Mengde memorialized to move the army of Commander-in-Chief Han Shiqing to garrison Jiankang, Cui Zeng to garrison Caishi, and Yan Gao to divide defense of strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: He moved Han Shiqing's forces into Jiankang, posted Cui Zeng at Caishi, and assigned Yan Gao to hold key positions.

sentences.zh: 會王才降劉豫，引兵入寇，夢得遣使臣張偉諭才降之，以其眾分隸諸軍。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Cai had surrendered to Liu Yu and led troops in to raid; Mengde sent envoy Zhang Wei to instruct Cai to surrender, and distributed his forces among the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Cai, who had defected to Liu Yu, led a raid, Mengde sent Zhang Wei to induce his surrender and distributed his troops among the regular armies.

sentences.zh: 濠、壽叛將寇 宏、陳卞雖陽受朝命，陰與劉豫通，夢得諭以福禍，皆聽命。

translations.literal: The rebel generals of Hao and Shou, Kou Hong and Chen Bi, though outwardly accepting court orders, secretly communicated with Liu Yu; Mengde instructed them on fortune and disaster, and all obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The defectors Kou Hong and Chen Bi of Hao and Shou nominally accepted imperial orders but secretly dealt with Liu Yu. Mengde warned them of the consequences, and both submitted.

sentences.zh: 及豫入寇，卞擊敗之，齊兵宵遁。

translations.literal: When Yu invaded, Bi defeated him and the Qi army fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu invaded, Chen Bi routed him and the Qi forces fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 八年，除江東安撫製置大使兼知建康府、行宮留守。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made Grand Commissioner for Pacification and Defense of Jiangdong and concurrently prefect of Jiankang and keeper of the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In 1138 he was appointed Grand Commissioner for Pacification and Defense of Jiangdong, prefect of Jiankang, and keeper of the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 又 奏防江措畫八事：一、申飭邊備，二、分布地分，三、把截要害，四、約束舟船，五、團結鄉社，六、明審斥堠，七、措置積聚，八、責官吏死守。

translations.literal: He also memorialized eight measures for defending the river: first, tighten border preparations; second, distribute territorial divisions; third, block strategic points; fourth, restrain boats and ships; fifth, organize village militia; sixth, clarify scout posts; seventh, arrange stockpiles; eighth, charge officials and clerks to defend to the death.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed eight measures for river defense: tighten border discipline, distribute forces, hold choke points, control shipping, organize local militia, clarify scouting, stockpile supplies, and require officials to defend their posts to the death.

sentences.zh: 又言建康、太 平、池州緊要隘口、江北可濟渡去處共一十九處，願聚集民兵，把截要害，命諸將審度敵形，並力進討。

translations.literal: He also said that at Jiankang, Taiping, and Chizhou there were nineteen critical passes and places on the north bank where crossing was possible; he wished to gather militia, block strategic points, and order the generals to assess the enemy's form and join strength to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: He identified nineteen critical crossings along the Jiankang-Taiping-Chizhou line and on the north bank, urged assembling militia to hold them, and ordered generals to coordinate a joint offensive after assessing enemy movements.

sentences.zh: 金都元帥宗弼犯含山縣，進逼曆陽，張俊諸軍 遷延未發，夢得見俊，請速出軍，曰：“敵已過含山縣，萬一金人得和州，長江不可保矣。”

translations.literal: The Jin Grand Marshal Zongbi attacked Hanshan County and pressed on toward Liyang; Zhang Jun's armies delayed and did not march. Mengde saw Jun and begged him to advance quickly, saying: "The enemy has already passed Hanshan County; if by any chance the Jin obtain Hezhou, the Yangtze cannot be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin generalissimo Zongbi attacked Hanshan County and pressed Liyang, Zhang Jun's armies lingered. Mengde urged him to send out the armies quickly: "The enemy has already passed Hanshan County. If by chance the Jin take Hezhou, the Yangtze cannot be secured."

sentences.zh: 俊趣諸軍進發，聲勢大振，金兵退屯昭關。

translations.literal: Jun urged the armies to advance; their momentum greatly revived, and the Jin troops withdrew to garrison at Zhaoguan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun hurried his armies forward. Their momentum revived, and the Jin fell back to Zhaoguan.

sentences.zh: 明年，金復入寇，遂至柘 皋，夢得團結沿江民兵數萬，分據江津，遣子模將千人守馬家渡，金兵不得渡而去。

translations.literal: The next year the Jin again invaded and reached Zhegao. Mengde organized tens of thousands of militia along the river, divided occupation of river crossings, and sent his son Mo with a thousand men to defend Majia Ford; the Jin army could not cross and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Jin invaded again as far as Zhegao. Mengde rallied tens of thousands of river militia, seized the crossings, and sent his son Mo with a thousand men to hold Majia Ford. The Jin could not cross and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，建康屯兵歲費錢八百萬緡，米八十萬斛，榷貨務所入不足以支。

translations.literal: Initially the garrison at Jiankang yearly cost eight million strings of cash and eight hundred thousand hu of rice; the income of the Monopoly Bureau was insufficient to support it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiankang garrison had cost eight million strings and eight hundred thousand hu of rice annually, more than the Monopoly Bureau could supply.

sentences.zh: 至是，禁旅與諸道兵鹹集，夢得兼總四路漕計以給饋餉，軍用不乏，故諸將得悉力以戰。

translations.literal: By this time the palace guard and armies of the various circuits all gathered; Mengde concurrently oversaw the transport accounts of four circuits to supply provisions, and military use was not lacking, so the generals could exert their full strength in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace guard and provincial armies converged, Mengde took charge of transport from four circuits. Supplies held, and the generals could fight at full strength.

sentences.zh: 詔加觀文殿學士，移知福州，兼福建安撫使。

translations.literal: An edict added Academician of the Guanwen Hall; he was transferred to govern Fuzhou and concurrently made Pacification Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician of the Guanwen Hall and transferred to Fuzhou as prefect and Pacification Commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 海寇朱明猖獗，詔夢得挾御前將士便道之鎮，或招或捕，或誘之相戕，遂平寇五十餘群。

translations.literal: The sea bandit Zhu Ming ran rampant; an edict ordered Mengde to take imperial guards by express route to the prefecture, recruiting or capturing or enticing them to kill one another, and he thus pacified more than fifty bandit groups.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirate Zhu Ming ravaged the coast, Mengde was ordered to take imperial guards to Fujian by express route. By recruiting, capturing, and setting bandits against one another, he suppressed more than fifty bands.

sentences.zh: 然頗與監司異議，上章請老，特遷一官，提舉臨安府洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Yet he rather often differed in opinion from supervisory commissioners; he submitted a memorial requesting retirement, was specially promoted one rank, and made superintendent of the Dongxiao Abbey in Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed frequently with supervisory commissioners, petitioned to retire, received a special promotion, and was made superintendent of the Dongxiao Abbey near Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 尋拜崇信軍節度使致仕。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Military Commissioner of Chongxin Army and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired with the title Military Commissioner of Chongxin.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒湖州，贈檢校少保。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died at Huzhou; posthumously granted Acting Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Huzhou in 1148 and was posthumously granted Acting Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 程俱，字致道，衢州開化人。

translations.literal: Cheng Ju, styled Zhidao, was a native of Kaihua in Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ju, whose style name was Zhidao, came from Kaihua in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 以外祖尚書左丞鄧潤甫恩，補蘇州吳江主簿，監舒州太湖茶場，坐上書論事罷歸。

translations.literal: On the privilege of his maternal grandfather Left Vice Director Deng Runfu he was appointed registrar of Wujiang in Suzhou, supervised the Taihu tea plantation in Shuzhou, and was dismissed and sent home for memorializing on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Through his maternal grandfather, Left Vice Director Deng Runfu, he became registrar of Wujiang in Suzhou and superintendent of the Taihu tea plantation in Shuzhou, but was dismissed after memorializing on policy.

sentences.zh: 起知泗州臨淮縣，累遷將作監丞。

translations.literal: He was raised to govern Linhuai County in Sizhou and was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as magistrate of Linhuai in Sizhou and rose to Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 近臣以詵述薦，遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: A court intimate recommended him for exposition and narration; he was transferred to Assistant Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A court intimate recommended his literary talent, and he was made Assistant Compiler.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，進頌，賜上舍出身，除禮部郎，以病告老，不俟報而歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe he presented a eulogy, was granted Upper College status, appointed Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, pleaded illness to retire, and returned home without awaiting reply.
translations.idiomatic: In 1120 he presented a court eulogy, received Upper College standing, and was made Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, but retired on grounds of illness without waiting for approval.

sentences.zh: 建炎中，為太常少卿、知秀州。

translations.literal: During Jianyan he was Vice Minister of Rites and prefect of Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyan era he served as Vice Minister of Rites and prefect of Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會車駕臨幸，賜對。

translations.literal: It happened that the imperial carriage visited; he was granted an audience.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession visited, he was granted an audience.

sentences.zh: 俱言：“陛下德日新，政日舉，賞罰施置，仰當天意，俯合人心，則趙氏安而社稷固；

translations.literal: Ju said: "Your Majesty's virtue renews daily and government advances daily; rewards, punishments, and appointments, looking up should match Heaven's intent and looking down should accord with people's hearts—then the house of Zhao is secure and the altars of soil and grain are firm;"
translations.idiomatic: Ju said, "If Your Majesty's virtue and governance advance daily, and rewards and punishments align with Heaven above and the people's hearts below, the Zhao house will be secure and the realm firm;

sentences.zh: 不然，則宗社危而天下 亂，其間蓋不容發。”

translations.literal: "otherwise the ancestral altars are in peril and all under Heaven is in chaos—between these there is no room for the breadth of a hair."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise the altars will totter and the realm fall into chaos—and between the two lies no margin at all."

sentences.zh: 高宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: Gaozong praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong praised his counsel.

sentences.zh: 金兵南渡，據臨安，遣兵破崇德、海鹽，馳檄諭降。

translations.literal: Jin troops crossed south, occupied Lin'an, sent troops to break Chongde and Haiyan, and dispatched rapid proclamations ordering surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jin forces crossed the river, seized Lin'an, attacked Chongde and Haiyan, and sent urgent summons to surrender.

sentences.zh: 俱率官屬棄城保華亭，留兵馬都監守城。

translations.literal: Ju led his subordinate officials to abandon the city and defend at Huating, leaving the cavalry and infantry commander to guard the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ju led his staff out of the city to Huating, leaving the military inspector to hold Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命俱部金帛赴行在，既至，以 病乞歸。

translations.literal: The court ordered Ju to escort gold and silks to the traveling palace; once he arrived he pleaded illness and begged to return.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered him to escort gold and silks to the traveling palace. After delivering them he pleaded illness and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，始置秘書省，召俱為少監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxing the Secretariat was first established; Ju was summoned as Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat was re-established early in Shaoxing, Ju was summoned as its Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 奏修日曆，秘書長貳得預修纂，自俱始。

translations.literal: He memorialized to compile the Calendar; senior Secretariat officials were allowed to take part in compilation—this began with Ju.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to compile the Calendar, establishing the precedent that senior Secretariat officials could take part in historical compilation.

sentences.zh: 時庶事草創，百司文書例從省記，俱摭三館舊聞，比次為書，名 曰《麟台故事》上之。

translations.literal: At that time numerous affairs were newly founded; the documents of the hundred offices customarily followed Secretariat records. Ju gathered old reports of the Three Halls, arranged them in order into a book, titled 《Records of the Lin Terrace》, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: With government still being rebuilt, ministries relied on Secretariat records. Ju compiled old reports from the Three Halls into the 《Records of the Lin Terrace》 and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 擢中書舍人兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and concurrently Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 俱論：“國家之患，在於論事者不敢盡情，當事者不敢任責，言有用否，事有成敗，理固不齊。

translations.literal: Ju argued: "The state's affliction lies in this: those who discuss affairs dare not speak fully, and those who handle affairs dare not bear responsibility. Whether words are useful or not, whether affairs succeed or fail—the principle is inherently not uniform."
translations.idiomatic: Ju argued: "The state's trouble lies in advisers not daring to speak frankly and officials not daring to accept responsibility. Counsel may be right or wrong and policies may succeed or fail—that is naturally uneven.

sentences.zh: 今言不合則見排於當時， 事不諧則追咎於始議。

translations.literal: Now if words do not accord one is rejected in the present; if affairs do not succeed blame is traced to the first proposer.
translations.idiomatic: Today dissent is punished immediately, and failed policies are blamed on whoever proposed them first.

sentences.zh: 故雖有智如陳平，不敢請金以行間；

translations.literal: Therefore even one as wise as Chen Ping dares not ask for gold to conduct stratagems;
translations.idiomatic: Thus even a man as clever as Chen Ping would not dare ask for gold to run espionage;

sentences.zh: 勇如相如，不敢全璧以抗秦；

translations.literal: as brave as Xiangru dares not keep the jade intact to resist Qin;
translations.idiomatic: nor one as bold as Lin Xiangru risk keeping the jade whole to defy Qin;

sentences.zh: 通財如劉晏，不敢言理財以贍軍食。

translations.literal: as versed in finance as Liu Yan dares not speak of managing wealth to provision the army.
translations.idiomatic: nor one as skilled in finance as Liu Yan propose managing revenues to feed the armies.

sentences.zh: 使人人不敢當事，不敢盡謀，則艱危之 時，誰與圖回而恢復乎？”

translations.literal: If everyone dares not handle affairs and dares not offer full counsel, then in times of hardship and peril, who will plan restoration with you?
translations.idiomatic: If no one dares take responsibility or speak fully, who in such desperate times will help plan recovery?"

sentences.zh: 武功大夫蘇易轉橫行，俱論：“祖宗之法，文臣自將作監主簿至尚書左仆射，武臣自三班奉職至節度使，此以次遷轉之官 也。

translations.literal: Martial Achievement Grandee Su Yi was transferred to lateral rank. Ju argued: "By the law of the ancestral emperors, for civil officials from Registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and for military officials from Third Class Attendant to Military Commissioner—these are offices transferred in sequence."
translations.idiomatic: When Martial Accomplishment Grandee Su Yi was moved to lateral rank, Ju argued: "Under the law of the ancestors, civil officials from Registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and military officials from Third Class Attendant for Service to military commissioner, were offices advanced through in proper sequence.

sentences.zh: 武臣自閣門副使至內客省使為橫行，不係磨勘遷轉之列，其除授皆頒特旨。

translations.literal: For military officials, from Vice Commissioner of the Palace Gate to Commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau were lateral ranks, not in the series of merit review and sequential transfer; their appointments and grants all issued by special edict.
translations.idiomatic: Military lateral ranks from Vice Commissioner of the Palace Gate to Commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau lay outside the merit-review ladder and required special edicts.

sentences.zh: 故元豐之製，以承務郎至特進為寄祿官，易監主簿至仆射之名；

translations.literal: Therefore the Yuanfeng system made from Court Gentleman to Special Advancement the salary-rank offices, changing the names from registrar to vice director;
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanfeng reforms therefore made Court Gentleman through Special Advancement salary ranks, renaming posts from registrar through vice director;

sentences.zh: 武臣獨不以寄祿官易 之者，蓋有深意也。

translations.literal: for military officials alone they did not replace posts with salary-rank offices—this surely had deep meaning.
translations.idiomatic: but deliberately did not apply salary ranks to military posts—a measure of deep significance.

sentences.zh: 政和間，改武臣官稱為郎、大夫，遂並橫行易之為轉官等級，蓋當時有司不習典故，以開僥幸之門。

translations.literal: During Zhenghe they changed military officials' titles to Gentleman and Grandee, and thereby merged lateral ranks into the grades of sequential transfer—surely the officials of the time did not study precedents and opened a gate to undeserved fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenghe military titles were renamed as Gentleman and Grandee, folding lateral ranks into the regular ladder—ignorance of precedent that opened the door to favoritism.

sentences.zh: 自改使為大夫以來，常調之官，下至皂隸， 轉為橫行者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Since changing commissioner to grandee, regular-route officials down to clerks and runners transferred to lateral rank beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Since commissioners were renamed grandees, countless routine officials—even clerks—have been shifted into lateral ranks.

sentences.zh: 且文臣所謂庶官者，轉不得過中大夫，而武臣乃得過皇城使，此何理也！

translations.literal: Moreover, among civil officials called subordinate officers, transfer cannot pass Grandee of Governance, yet military officials can pass Commissioner of the Imperial City—what principle is this!
translations.idiomatic: Civil subordinates cannot rise above Grandee of Governance, yet military officers can rise above Commissioner of the Imperial City. What principle is that?

sentences.zh: 夫官職輕重在朝廷，朝廷愛重官職，不妄與人，則官職重；

translations.literal: The weight of office lies with the court; when the court cherishes and esteems office and does not give it rashly to people, then office is weighty;
translations.idiomatic: Whether offices carry weight depends on the court. When the court values them and grants them sparingly, they remain weighty;

sentences.zh: 反是則 輕，輕則得者不以為恩，未得者常懷觖望，此安危治亂所關也。”

translations.literal: if the reverse, they are light; if light, those who obtain them do not regard them as grace, and those who do not obtain them constantly harbor resentment—this is what security and danger, order and chaos depend upon.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise they become cheap. Cheap offices bring no gratitude to recipients and breed resentment in those passed over—matters on which safety and ruin depend."

sentences.zh: 徐俯為諫議大夫，俱繳還，以為：“俯雖才俊氣豪，所曆尚淺，以前任省郎，遽除諫 議，自元豐更製以來，未之有也。

translations.literal: Xu Fu was made Remonstrance Grandee; Ju returned the appointment, stating: "Though Fu is talented, spirited, and bold, his experience is still shallow. From his former post as provincial gentleman he was suddenly made remonstrance official—since the Yuanfeng reforms there has been nothing like it."
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Fu was appointed Remonstrance Grandee, Ju returned the edict, arguing: "Though Fu is talented and bold, his experience is still shallow. To leap from provincial gentleman to remonstrance official is unprecedented since Yuanfeng.

sentences.zh: 昔唐元稹為荊南判司，忽命從中出，召為省郎，使知制誥，遂喧朝聽，時謂監軍崔潭峻之所引也。

translations.literal: Formerly in Tang, Yuan Zhen was a judicial aide in Jingnan; suddenly an order issued from within, summoning him as provincial gentleman and making him drafter of edicts—the court was immediately in uproar, and at the time it was said he was introduced by the army supervisor Cui Tanjun.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang, Yuan Zhen was a mere aide in Jingnan when a sudden inner order made him a provincial drafter—throwing the court into uproar as a protégé of the army supervisor Cui Tanjun.

sentences.zh: 近聞外傳，俯與中官唱和，有‘ 魚須’之句，號為警策。

translations.literal: Recently it is heard abroad that Fu exchanges verses with inner eunuchs; there is a line on 'fish whiskers' praised as striking and alert.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors abroad say Fu exchanges poetry with palace eunuchs, including a celebrated line on 'fish whiskers.'

sentences.zh: 臣恐外人以此為疑，仰累聖德。

translations.literal: Your servant fears outsiders will take this as grounds for suspicion and thereby burden Your sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: I fear outsiders will suspect impropriety and cast doubt on Your Majesty's virtue.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠知俯，姑以所應得者命之。”

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly knows Fu, for the moment grant him what he ought to receive."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly values Fu, appoint him only to the rank he has earned."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not respond.

sentences.zh: 後二日，言者論俱前棄秀州城，罷為提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: Two days later memorialists discussed Ju's earlier abandonment of Xiuzhou city; he was dismissed to superintendent of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later critics cited his abandonment of Xiuzhou, and he was dismissed to superintendent of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，除 徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made Attendant Drafter of the Huixuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made Attendant Drafter of the Huixuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 俱晚病風痹，秦檜薦俱領史事，除提舉萬壽觀、實錄院修撰，使免朝參，俱力辭不至。

translations.literal: Ju in his later years suffered from wind paralysis; Qin Hui recommended Ju to head historical affairs, appointing him superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey and Veritable Record compiler, exempting him from court attendance—Ju strenuously declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In later life Ju suffered from paralysis. Qin Hui recommended him to head historical compilation as superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey and Veritable Record compiler with exemption from court attendance. Ju firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 俱在掖垣，命令下有不安於心者，必反覆言之，不少畏避。

translations.literal: When Ju was in the Secretariat precinct, if an order issued below disquieted his heart he would speak of it repeatedly and not shrink from fear.
translations.idiomatic: In the Secretariat, whenever an edict troubled him he spoke against it repeatedly, without fear.

sentences.zh: 其為文典雅閎奧，為世所稱。

translations.literal: His writing was elegant, refined, broad, and profound, and was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was elegant and profound, and widely admired.

sentences.zh: 張嵲，字巨山，襄陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei, styled Jushan, was a native of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei, whose style name was Jushan, came from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 宣和三年，上舍選中第。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuanhe he was selected in the Upper College examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1121 he passed the Upper College examination.

sentences.zh: 調唐州方城尉，改房州司刑曹。

translations.literal: He was assigned as magistrate of Fangcheng in Tangzhou, then changed to judicial officer of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as magistrate of Fangcheng in Tangzhou, then made judicial officer of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉子羽薦於川、陝宣撫使張浚，辟利州路安撫司幹辦公事，以母病去官。

translations.literal: Liu Ziyu recommended him to the Sichuan-Shaanxi Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun; he was recruited as clerk for general affairs in the Lizhou Pacification Office and left office because his mother was ill.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ziyu recommended him to Zhang Jun, pacification commissioner of Sichuan and Shaanxi. He served as clerk in the Lizhou Pacification Office but left when his mother fell ill.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，召對，嵲上疏曰：“金人去冬深涉吾地，王師屢捷，一朝宵遁，金有自敗之道，非我幸勝之也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing he was summoned for an audience; Wei memorialized: "Last winter the Jin deeply penetrated our territory; the imperial armies repeatedly won victories, then one morning fled by night—the Jin had a path of self-defeat; it was not that we luckily prevailed."
translations.idiomatic: In 1135 he was summoned to audience and memorialized: "Last winter the Jin penetrated deep into our territory. Our armies won repeated victories, then the Jin fled overnight. They defeated themselves; we did not merely get lucky.

sentences.zh: 今士氣稍振，乘其銳而用之；

translations.literal: Now morale is somewhat revived; riding their keen edge to employ it;
translations.idiomatic: Morale has revived somewhat, and it is tempting to strike while enthusiasm is high;

sentences.zh: 固無不可。

translations.literal: there is certainly nothing impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: that is not impossible in itself.

sentences.zh: 然兵疲民勞， 若便圖進取，似未可遽。

translations.literal: Yet the troops are weary and the people exhausted; if one immediately plans advance and seizure, it seems it cannot be hurried.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the armies are weary and the people exhausted, and an immediate offensive seems premature.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂為今日計，當築塢堡以守淮南之地，興屯田以為久戍之資，備舟楫以阻長江之險，以我之常，待彼之變。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that for today's plan one should build walled forts to defend the Huainan lands, establish military colonies as resources for long garrison, prepare boats and oars to block the Yangtze's peril, and with our constancy await their changes.
translations.idiomatic: I believe we should build fortified posts to hold Huainan, establish military colonies for long-term defense, ready the fleet to control the Yangtze, and with steady preparation await the enemy's next move.

sentences.zh: 又荊、襄、壽春皆古重鎮， 敵之侵軼，多出此途。

translations.literal: Moreover Jing, Xiang, and Shouchun are all ancient strategic strongholds; the enemy's raids and incursions mostly come by these routes.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, Xiang, and Shouchun are ancient strategic centers, and most enemy raids come through them.

sentences.zh: 願速擇良將勁兵，戍守其地，以重上流之勢。”

translations.literal: I wish quickly to select good generals and strong troops to garrison and defend those places, thereby strengthening the upper reaches' posture."
translations.idiomatic: I urge swift selection of able generals and strong troops to garrison them and secure the upper Yangtze."

sentences.zh: 召試，除秘書省正字。

translations.literal: He was summoned for examination and made Corrector of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was examined and appointed Corrector of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 六年，地震。

translations.literal: In the sixth year there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In 1136 there was an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 嵲奏：“比年以來，賦斂繁重，征求百出，流移者擠溝壑，土著者失常業，地震之異，殆或為此。

translations.literal: Wei memorialized: "In recent years tax levies have been heavy and collections emerge in a hundred forms; the displaced crowd ditches and gullies, and the settled lose their regular occupations—the anomaly of the earthquake is perhaps because of this."
translations.idiomatic: Wei memorialized: "In recent years taxes and exactions have multiplied, driving refugees into ditches and ruining settled livelihoods; the earthquake likely stems from this.

sentences.zh: 願深思變異之由，修政之闕，致民之安。”

translations.literal: I wish deeply to ponder the source of anomalies, repair the gaps in government, and bring the people to peace.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to ponder the cause of such omens, correct failures in governance, and restore the people's peace."

sentences.zh: 七年，遷校書郎兼史館校勘，再遷著作郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Collator and concurrently History Office proofreader, and again transferred to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1137 he was made Collator and History Office proofreader, then Compiler.

sentences.zh: 嵲因對言：“吳、蜀，唇齒之勢也。

translations.literal: Wei, responding in audience, said: "Wu and Shu are in a lip-and-teeth relationship."
translations.idiomatic: In audience Wei replied: "Wu and Shu stand in the same lip-and-teeth alliance.

sentences.zh: 蜀去朝廷遠，今無元帥一年矣。

translations.literal: Shu is far from the court; now there has been no commander-in-chief for a year.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan is distant from the court, and the region has gone a year without a supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 蜀之利害，臣粗知之。

translations.literal: The advantages and disadvantages of Shu—your servant has a rough knowledge of them.
translations.idiomatic: I have some understanding of what is at stake in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 忠勇之人，使之捍外侮則 可，至於撫循斯民，則非所能辦也。

translations.literal: Loyal and brave men may be made to repel foreign insult—that is acceptable; as for comforting and guiding these people, that is not something they can accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and loyal men can defend against foreign aggression, but they cannot govern and care for the local population.

sentences.zh: 宜於前宰執中，擇其可以任川事者委任之。

translations.literal: Among former chief ministers one should select those able to undertake Sichuan affairs and entrust them.
translations.idiomatic: The court should choose from among former chief ministers someone capable of handling Sichuan affairs and appoint him.

sentences.zh: 然川蜀係國利害，非腹心之臣不可，今早得一賢宣撫使為要。”

translations.literal: Yet Sichuan is bound up with the state's advantage and harm—not a trusted inner minister will not do; what is essential today is promptly obtaining one worthy Pacification Commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: But Sichuan bears directly on the nation's fortunes, so only a trusted inner minister will do—and the urgent need now is to find a worthy Pacification Commissioner."

sentences.zh: 又言：“自駐蹕吳會 以來，似未嚐以襄陽、荊南為意，今宜亟選儒臣有牧禦之才者為二路帥，使之招集流散，興農桑，治城壁，以為保固之資，益重上流之勢。”

translations.literal: He also said: "Since taking up residence in the Wu commanderies, it seems one has not yet taken Xiangyang and Jingnan to heart; now one should urgently select scholarly officials with the talent to govern and defend as commanders of the two circuits, having them gather the scattered, promote agriculture and sericulture, repair walls and ramparts, as resources for secure defense, and further strengthen the posture of the upper reaches."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Since the court settled in the southeast, Xiangyang and southern Jing seem to have received too little attention. The court should quickly appoint learned officials with governing and defensive ability to command both circuits, to gather refugees, revive farming, repair fortifications, build a secure base, and strengthen the upper Yangtze."

sentences.zh: 既而何掄 以刊改《神宗實錄》得罪，語連嵲，出為福建路轉運判官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward He Lun was punished for revising the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong》; his words implicated Wei, who was sent out as Vice Transport Commissioner of Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward He Lun was punished for altering the Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong; his case implicated Wei, who was demoted to Vice Transport Commissioner of Fujian Circuit.

sentences.zh: 上疏略曰：“古之人君，其患有二，不在於拒諫，在納諫而不能用；

translations.literal: In a memorial he briefly said: "Ancient rulers had two afflictions: not in rejecting remonstrance, but in accepting remonstrance yet being unable to use it;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial in summary: "Ancient rulers suffered from two faults—not refusing advice, but accepting it and then failing to act on it;

sentences.zh: 不在於不知天下利害，在知而不以為 意。

translations.literal: not in not knowing the world's advantages and harm, but in knowing yet not taking it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: not in ignorance of what helps or harms the realm, but in knowing and yet not caring.

sentences.zh: 陛下渡江十年矣，外有敵之國，內有驕悍之兵，下有窮困無聊之民。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has crossed the Yangtze ten years now; outwardly there is an enemy state, inwardly there are proud and fierce troops, below there are destitute and despairing people.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has been south of the Yangtze for ten years. Abroad there is a hostile power, at home unruly troops, and below a people driven to destitution and despair.

sentences.zh: 進言者多矣，今皆以為陳腐而別取新奇之說；

translations.literal: Those who advance counsel are many; now all are deemed stale and one separately adopts novel doctrines;
translations.idiomatic: Many have offered counsel, yet sound advice is dismissed as stale while novel theories are sought instead;

sentences.zh: 任事者眾矣，今皆習是以為當然而更為迂闊之 事。

translations.literal: Those who undertake affairs are numerous; now all take habit as what is proper yet do more far-fetched things.
translations.idiomatic: many hold office, yet routine is mistaken for wisdom while ever more impractical schemes are pursued.

sentences.zh: 此近於納諫而不知用，知利害而不知恤也。
