translations.literal: This approximates accepting remonstrance yet not knowing how to use it, knowing advantage and harm yet not knowing sympathy.
translations.idiomatic: This comes close to hearing advice without using it, and knowing what matters without truly caring.

sentences.zh: 為今之計，朝斯夕斯，非是二者不務，數年之後，庶其有濟！

translations.literal: For today's plan, morning and evening, let nothing but these two be pursued—after several years perhaps there will be success!
translations.idiomatic: For the present, let the court devote itself morning and night to nothing else. In a few years there may yet be hope!

sentences.zh: 有國之所惡者，莫大於朋黨，今一宰相用，凡其所與 者，不擇賢否而盡用之，一宰相去，凡其所與者，不擇賢否而盡逐之，宜其朋黨之浸成也。”

translations.literal: What a state most detests is nothing greater than factions; now when one chief minister is employed, all whom he associates with—without choosing whether worthy or not—are all employed; when one chief minister departs, all whom he associates with—without choosing whether worthy or not—are all driven out. No wonder factions gradually form.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing harms a state more than factionalism. When one chief minister takes power, all his associates are appointed regardless of merit; when he falls, all are purged regardless of merit. Small wonder factions keep growing."

sentences.zh: 九年，除司勳員外郎兼實錄院檢討官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently Veritable Record Office compiler-reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1139 he was made Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel and compiler-reviewer at the Veritable Record Office.

sentences.zh: 金人叛盟，上命兩 省、卿、監、郎、曹各草檄以進，獨取嵲所進者，播之四方。

translations.literal: The Jurchens broke the treaty; the emperor ordered both secretariats, ministers, supervisors, bureau chiefs, and clerks each to draft proclamations to submit—only Wei's submission was selected and broadcast throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens broke the treaty, the emperor ordered officials throughout both secretariats to draft proclamations. Only Wei's was chosen and published across the realm.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢中書舍人，升實錄院同修撰。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and advanced to co-compiler of the Veritable Record Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1140 he was promoted to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and co-compiler of the Veritable Record Office.

sentences.zh: 論王德收復宿、亳兩郡，乃擅退軍，使岳飛勢孤，金人猖獗，授 承宣防禦使，何應罰而反賞？

translations.literal: Memorializing that Wang De recovered Su and Bo prefectures yet on his own authority withdrew troops, leaving Yue Fei isolated while the Jurchens grew rampant—yet he was granted the rank of Defense Commissioner: why should punishment be due yet reward given instead?
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Wang De had recovered Su and Bo but then withdrew on his own authority, leaving Yue Fei isolated and the Jurchens emboldened—yet Wang was rewarded with the rank of Defense Commissioner. Why punish when one should reward, or reward when one should punish?

sentences.zh: 封還詞頭，乞罷已降轉官指揮。

translations.literal: He sealed and returned the draft commission, requesting cancellation of the already issued order for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He returned the draft appointment and asked that the promotion order be revoked.

sentences.zh: 未幾，右正言万俟卨論嵲為侍從日，薦引非才，以酬私恩，邊報始至，托疾家居，由是罷去。

translations.literal: Before long, Right Remonstrance Officer Wan Qixie memorialized that when Wei was in attendance he had recommended unqualified men to repay private favor; when frontier reports first arrived he feigned illness and stayed home—thereby he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Right Remonstrance Officer Wan Qixie accused Wei of recommending unworthy men to repay private favors while in court service, and of feigning illness at home when frontier reports first arrived. Wei was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，起 知衢州，除敷文閣待制。

translations.literal: Before long he was reappointed to govern Quzhou and made Awaiting-Edict of the Fuwen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was reappointed prefect of Quzhou and made Awaiting-Edict of the Fuwen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 為政頗尚嚴酷，歲滿，得請提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: His governance leaned rather toward severity; when his term ended he obtained leave to superintend the Taiping Xingguo Abbey of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was notably harsh. When his term ended he requested appointment as superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時方修好息兵，朝廷講稽古禮文之事，嵲作《中興復古詩》以進。

translations.literal: At the time peace was being restored and arms laid down; the court was examining ancient ritual and documents—Wei composed the 《Poems on Restoring Antiquity in the Restoration》 and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had been restored and the court was reviving ancient ritual and scholarship. Wei composed the Poems on Restoring Antiquity in the Restoration and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上將召用，會疽發背 卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to summon and employ him when he happened to die of a carbuncle on the back, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to recall him to office when he died of a back abscess at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 子昌時。

translations.literal: His son was Changshi.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Changshi.

sentences.zh: 韓駒，字子蒼，仙井監人。

translations.literal: Han Ju, styled Zicang, was a native of Xianjing Superintendency.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ju, whose style name was Zicang, came from Xianjing Superintendency.

sentences.zh: 少有文稱。

translations.literal: From youth he had a reputation for literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for literary talent from an early age.

sentences.zh: 政和初，以獻頌補假將仕郎，召試舍人院，賜進士出身，除秘書省正字。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenghe, by submitting a eulogy he received the provisional rank of Gentleman for Merit, was summoned for examination at the Drafting Academy, granted jinshi standing, and appointed Secretariat Corrector.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhenghe era he earned provisional rank by submitting a eulogy, passed the Drafting Academy examination, received jinshi standing, and was appointed Secretariat Corrector.

sentences.zh: 尋坐為蘇氏 學，請監華州蒲城縣市易務。

translations.literal: Soon he was punished for Su-shi Learning and requested supervision of the market-trade office of Pucheng County, Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon punished for association with Su-shi Learning and requested appointment as supervisor of the market-trade office in Pucheng County, Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 知洪州分寧縣。

translations.literal: He governed Fenning County, Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Fenning County in Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 召為著作郎，校正御前文籍。

translations.literal: Summoned as Compiler and to collate imperial archives.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Compiler and assigned to collate the imperial archives.

sentences.zh: 駒言國家祠事，歲一百十有八，用樂者六十有二，舊撰樂章，辭多牴牾。

translations.literal: Ju stated that the state's sacrificial rites numbered one hundred eighteen per year, sixty-two using music; the old composed music texts had many contradictions.
translations.idiomatic: Ju reported that the state performed 118 sacrificial rites each year, 62 with music, and that the old hymn texts contained many inconsistencies.

sentences.zh: 於是詔三館士分 撰親祠明堂、圓壇、方澤等樂曲五十餘章，多駒所作。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor ordered Three Academies scholars to compose separately more than fifty chapters of music for personally sacrificing at the Bright Hall, Round Altar, Square Mound, and the like—mostly composed by Ju.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Three Academies scholars to compose more than fifty hymn texts for imperial sacrifices at the Bright Hall, Round Altar, and Square Mound, most of them written by Ju.

sentences.zh: 宣和五年，除秘書少監。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuanhe he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1123 he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷中書舍人兼修國史，入謝。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Drafting Attendant and concurrently national history compiler; he entered to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Drafting Attendant and national history compiler, and entered court to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 上曰：“近年為製誥者，所褒必溢 美，所貶必溢惡，豈王言之體。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In recent years those who compose edicts invariably overflow with praise when commending and overflow with evil when condemning—is this the form of kingly words?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "In recent years edict writers have lavished excessive praise on those commended and excessive condemnation on those censured. Is that the proper tone of royal pronouncements?

sentences.zh: 且《盤》、《誥》具在，寧若是乎？”

translations.literal: Moreover the 《Pan》 and 《Gao》 are fully extant—would it be like this?"
translations.idiomatic: The models of the Pan and Gao documents still survive—would they read like this?"

sentences.zh: 駒對：“若止作製誥，則粗知文墨者皆可為，先帝置兩省，豈止使行文書而已。”

translations.literal: Ju replied: "If one only writes edicts, then anyone roughly knowing letters can do it—the late emperor established the two secretariats surely not merely to circulate documents."
translations.idiomatic: Ju replied: "If drafting edicts were all that mattered, anyone with a rough knowledge of writing and documents could do the job. The late emperor did not establish the two secretariats merely to circulate paperwork."

sentences.zh: 上曰：“給 事實掌封駁。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Supervising Secretariat Attendants truly manage seal-and-rebuttal."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Supervising Secretariat Attendants are indeed charged with reviewing and rebutting edicts."

sentences.zh: 駒奏：“舍人亦許繳還詞頭。”

translations.literal: Ju memorialized: "Drafting attendants are also permitted to return draft commissions."
translations.idiomatic: Ju replied: "Drafting attendants are also allowed to return draft commissions for reconsideration."

sentences.zh: 上曰：“自今朝廷事有可論者，一切繳來。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "From now on, wherever court affairs are open to debate, return them all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "From now on, return any court matter you find objectionable."

sentences.zh: 尋兼權直學士院，製詞簡重，為時所推。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made acting director of the Hanlin Academy; his edict compositions were concise and weighty, and he was admired by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made acting director of the Hanlin Academy. His edicts were concise and dignified, and he was widely respected.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復坐鄉黨曲學，以集英 殿修撰提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: Before long he was again punished for partisan narrow learning and made Academy Compiler of the Jiying Hall, superintending the Taiping Abbey of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again punished for partisan narrow learning and made Academy Compiler of the Jiying Hall while superintending the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，知江州。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended, he was made prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Ju was appointed prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，卒於撫州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing he died at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Fuzhou in 1135.

sentences.zh: 進一官致仕，贈中奉大夫，與遺澤三人。

translations.literal: Promoted one rank upon retirement, posthumously granted Grandee of Palace Attendance, with hereditary privilege for three descendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted one rank upon retirement, posthumously granted Grandee of Palace Attendance, and given hereditary privilege for three descendants.

sentences.zh: 駒嚐在許下從蘇轍學，評其詩似儲光羲。

translations.literal: Ju had studied under Su Zhe at Xu and judged his poetry resembled Chu Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ju had studied under Su Zhe at Xu and remarked that his poetry resembled that of Chu Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 其後由宦者以進用，頗為識者所薄雲。

translations.literal: Afterward he advanced through eunuchs and was rather lightly regarded by the knowing—it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Later he rose through eunuch patronage, and knowledgeable contemporaries held him in low regard.

sentences.zh: 子遜、遊。

translations.literal: His sons were Xun and You.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons Xun and You.

sentences.zh: 朱敦儒

translations.literal: Zhu Dunru.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Dunru

sentences.zh: 朱敦儒，字希真，河南人。

translations.literal: Zhu Dunru, styled Xizhen, was a native of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Dunru, whose style name was Xizhen, came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 父勃，紹聖諫官。

translations.literal: His father Bo was a remonstrance officer under Shaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bo had served as a remonstrance officer under Emperor Zhezong.

sentences.zh: 敦儒誌行高潔，雖為布衣，而有朝野之望。

translations.literal: Dunru's integrity and conduct were lofty and pure; though a commoner he had reputation throughout court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Dunru was known for lofty integrity. Though a commoner, he enjoyed esteem both at court and beyond it.

sentences.zh: 靖康中，召至京師，將處以學官，敦儒辭曰：“麋鹿之性，自樂閑曠，爵 祿非所願也。”

translations.literal: During Jingkang he was summoned to the capital and was about to be given a scholarly post; Dunru declined: "The nature of deer is to delight in leisure and open wilds—rank and emolument are not what I wish."
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingkang crisis he was summoned to the capital and offered a scholarly post. Dunru declined: "Deer by nature love quiet and open country. Rank and salary are not what I want."

sentences.zh: 固辭還山。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and returned to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly refused and returned to the mountains.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，詔舉草澤才德之士，預選者命中書策試，授以官，於是淮西部使者言敦儒有文武才，召之。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended, an edict sought men of talent and virtue from the wilds; those pre-selected were ordered to written examination at the Secretariat and granted office. Thereupon the envoy of western Huai said Dunru had civil and military talent, and he was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne, an edict called for talented men from among the people. Those selected were examined at the Secretariat and given office. The envoy of western Huai then reported that Dunru possessed both civil and military ability, and he was summoned.

sentences.zh: 敦儒又辭。

translations.literal: Dunru again declined.
translations.idiomatic: Dunru declined again.

sentences.zh: 避亂客南雄州，張浚奏 赴軍前計議，弗起。

translations.literal: Fleeing turmoil he lodged at Nanxiong Prefecture; Zhang Jun memorialized that he come to military headquarters for consultation—he did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing the turmoil he stayed in Nanxiong Prefecture. Zhang Jun memorialized that he come to headquarters for consultation, but he did not go.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，宣諭使明橐言敦儒深達治體，有經世才，廷臣亦多稱其靖退。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, Persuasion Commissioner Ming Nang said Dunru deeply understood governance and had world-ordering talent; court ministers also often praised his tranquil withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: In 1132 Persuasion Commissioner Ming Nang reported that Dunru had a deep grasp of governance and talent for statecraft, and many court officials praised his quiet withdrawal from office.

sentences.zh: 詔以為右迪功郎，下肇慶府敦遣詣行在，敦儒不肯受詔。

translations.literal: An edict made him Right Assistant Gentleman for Merit; Zhaoqing Prefecture was ordered to escort him urgently to the traveling court—Dunru refused to accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Assistant Gentleman for Merit, and Zhaoqing Prefecture was ordered to escort him urgently to the traveling court. Dunru refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 其故人勸之曰：“今天子側席幽士，翼宣中興，譙定召於蜀，蘇庠召於浙，張自牧召於長蘆，莫不聲流天京，風動郡國，君何為棲茅茹藿，白首岩穀乎！”

translations.literal: His old friend urged him: "Today the Son of Heaven sits with folded mat for reclusive scholars to aid the Restoration—Qiao Ding was summoned from Shu, Su Kuang from Zhe, Zhang Zimu from Changlu—all without exception their fame flowed to the heavenly capital and their wind stirred commanderies and states—why do you dwell in thatched huts eating wild greens, white-haired in mountain valleys!"
translations.idiomatic: An old friend urged him: "The emperor now seeks out reclusive scholars to help restore the dynasty. Qiao Ding was summoned from Shu, Su Kuang from Zhe, Zhang Zimu from Changlu—all won fame at court and influence across the realm. Why should you live in a thatched hut on wild greens, growing old in the mountains?"

sentences.zh: 敦儒始幡 然而起。

translations.literal: Dunru then changed his mind and rose.
translations.idiomatic: At that Dunru changed his mind and accepted.

sentences.zh: 既至，命對便殿，論議明暢。

translations.literal: Once arrived he was ordered to audience in the informal hall; his discourse was clear and fluent.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he was granted audience in the informal hall, and his remarks were clear and persuasive.

sentences.zh: 上悅，賜進士出身，為秘書省正字。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, granted jinshi standing, and made him Secretariat Corrector.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, granted him jinshi standing, and appointed him Secretariat Corrector.

sentences.zh: 俄兼兵部郎官，遷兩浙東路提點刑獄。

translations.literal: Soon he additionally served as bureau chief of the Ministry of War and was transferred to Judicial Intendant of the Eastern Two Zhe Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served as bureau chief in the Ministry of War, then became Judicial Intendant of eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 會右諫議大夫汪勃劾敦儒專立異論，與李光交通。

translations.literal: When Right Remonstrance and Discussion Censor Wang Bo impeached Dunru for willfully setting up divergent opinions and associating with Li Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance and Discussion Censor Wang Bo then impeached Dunru for holding unorthodox views and associating with Li Guang.

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：“爵祿所以厲世，如其可與，則文臣便至侍從，武臣便至節鉞。

translations.literal: Gaozong said: "Rank and emolument serve to encourage the world—if one may be given them, then a civil official may straightway reach attendance, a military official straightway reach commander's seal.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong said: "Rank and salary exist to encourage public service. When a man deserves them, a civil official may rise straight to court attendance and a military man to command of armies.

sentences.zh: 如其不可，雖一命亦不容輕授。”

translations.literal: If one may not, then even one appointment cannot lightly be granted."
translations.idiomatic: When he does not deserve them, even the smallest appointment must not be granted lightly."

sentences.zh: 郭儒遂罷。

translations.literal: Dunru was thereupon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Dunru was thereupon dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十九年，上疏請歸，許之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he memorialized requesting retirement—permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1149 he memorialized asking to retire, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 郭儒素工詩及樂府，婉麗清暢。

translations.literal: Dunru had long excelled at poetry and yuefu—they were graceful, lovely, clear, and fluent.
translations.idiomatic: Dunru had long excelled at poetry and yuefu songs, which were graceful, lucid, and flowing.

sentences.zh: 時奏檜當國，喜獎用騷人墨客以文太平，檜子熺亦好詩，於是先用敦儒子為刪定官，復除敦儒鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: At the time Qin Hui held power; he liked to reward and employ poets and literary men to ornament peace—Qin Hui's son Xi also loved poetry—thereupon first employing Dunru's son as collation officer, then reappointing Dunru as Vice Minister of Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui dominated the government he liked to patronize poets and literary men to adorn an age of peace. Qin Hui's son Xi also loved poetry, so Dunru's son was first made a collation officer and Dunru himself was reappointed Vice Minister of Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 檜死，郭儒亦廢。

translations.literal: When Hui died, Dunru was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui died, Dunru was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 談者謂敦儒老懷舐犢之愛，而畏避竄逐，故其節不終雲。

translations.literal: Commentators said Dunru in old age harbored love like a cow licking its calf yet feared exile and dismissal—therefore his integrity was not sustained to the end, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators said that in old age Dunru indulged affection for his son while fearing exile, and so did not preserve his integrity to the end.

sentences.zh: 葛勝仲

translations.literal: Ge Shengzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Shengzhong

sentences.zh: 葛勝仲，字魯卿，丹陽人。

translations.literal: Ge Shengzhong, styled Luqing, was a native of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Shengzhong, whose style name was Luqing, came from Danyang.

sentences.zh: 登紹聖四年進士第，調杭州司理參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Shaosheng and was assigned as judicial administrator of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1097 and was assigned as judicial administrator of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 林希薦試學官及詞科，俱第一，除兗州教授，入為太學正。

translations.literal: Lin Xi recommended him for examination in academic and prose-poetry categories—both first; appointed professor of Yanzhou; entered as Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xi recommended him for the academic and prose-poetry examinations, and he placed first in both. He was appointed professor at Yanzhou and later became Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 上幸學，多獻頌者，勝仲獨獻賦，上 命中書第其優劣，勝仲為首，差提舉議曆所檢討官兼宗正丞。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the Academy many submitted eulogies—Shengzhong alone submitted a fu; the emperor ordered the Secretariat to rank their merit—Shengzhong was first and was assigned compiler-reviewer of the Calendar Reforms Office and concurrently Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Academy, most students submitted eulogies, but Shengzhong alone submitted a fu. The emperor ordered the Secretariat to rank the entries, and Shengzhong placed first. He was then made compiler-reviewer of the Calendar Reforms Office and Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 始，朝廷以從臣提舉議曆所，至是，代以郭天信，勝仲力請罷之。

translations.literal: Initially the court had had attendant ministers superintend the Calendar Reforms Office; at this point they replaced them with Guo Tianxin—Shengzhong strenuously requested abolishing this.
translations.idiomatic: At first attendant ministers had supervised the Calendar Reforms Office, but now Guo Tianxin was put in charge instead. Shengzhong strongly urged that the change be reversed.

sentences.zh: 稍遷禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 會御史中丞石公弼 言：“僖祖原廟增置殿室，違元豐之舊。”

translations.literal: When Censor-in-Chief Shi Gongbi said: "The primary temple of Emperor Xi added hall chambers, violating the Yuanfeng precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Shi Gongbi reported: "The addition of hall chambers to Emperor Xi's primary temple departs from the Yuanfeng precedent."

sentences.zh: 詔禮官議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered rites officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered rites officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 勝仲建言：“予而復奪，在常人猶難之，況在天之靈乎！”

translations.literal: Shengzhong proposed: "To grant then again withdraw—even for ordinary people it is hard; how much more for a spirit in Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Shengzhong argued: "To grant something and then take it back is hard even for ordinary people—how much more for an imperial ancestor in Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 議者非之，責知歙州休寧縣，復召為禮部員外郎， 權國子司業。

translations.literal: The debaters opposed him; he was demoted to govern Xiuning County, Shezhou; recalled as Outer Gentleman of Rites and acting Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His opponents prevailed, and he was demoted to magistrate of Xiuning County in Shezhou. Later he was recalled as Outer Gentleman of Rites and acting Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷命諸生習雅樂，樂成，進一官，遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: At the time the court ordered students to study elegant music; when the music was complete he was promoted one rank and transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ordered students to study court music and the project was completed, he was promoted one rank and made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 宋自建隆至治平所行典禮，歐陽修嚐裒集為書，凡百篇，號《太常因革禮》，詔勝仲 續之，增為三百卷，詔藏太常。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu had once compiled the rites practiced from Jianlong through Zhiping into a work of one hundred chapters titled Records of Rites Reforms at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. The emperor ordered Shengzhong to continue it, expanding it to three hundred juan, and commanded that it be kept at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu had once compiled the rites practiced from Jianlong through Zhiping into a work of one hundred chapters titled Records of Rites Reforms at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. The emperor ordered Shengzhong to continue it, expanding it to three hundred juan, and commanded that it be kept at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 及建春宮，以勝仲兼諭德，勝仲為《仁》、《孝》、《學》三論獻之太子，復采春秋、戰國以來曆代太子善惡成敗之跡，日進數事。

translations.literal: When the crown prince's residence was established, Shengzhong was made Preceptor. He wrote three treatises On Benevolence, On Filial Piety, and On Learning and presented them to the crown prince. He also collected examples from the Spring and Autumn period through the Warring States onward of crown princes' successes and failures, submitting several each day.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince's residence was established, Shengzhong was made Preceptor. He wrote three treatises On Benevolence, On Filial Piety, and On Learning and presented them to the crown prince. He also collected examples from the Spring and Autumn period through the Warring States onward of crown princes' successes and failures, submitting several each day.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉之，徙太府少卿，除國子祭酒，尋知汝州。

translations.literal: An edict praised him; he was moved to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, appointed Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, soon made prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him by edict, transferred him to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, appointed him Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, and soon made him prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 李彥括田，破產者眾，勝仲請蠲不當括者，彥怒，劾勝仲，上寢其奏，改湖州，尋徙鄧州。

translations.literal: Li Yan's land surveys bankrupted many; Shengzhong requested remission for those wrongly surveyed—Yan was angry and impeached Shengzhong; the emperor shelved the memorial; he was transferred to Huzhou, soon moved to Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan's land surveys ruined many households. Shengzhong asked that improper seizures be remitted. Yan angrily impeached him, but the emperor shelved the accusation and transferred Shengzhong to Huzhou, then soon to Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 朱勔先求白雀之屬，勝仲 不與，至是媒蘖其短，罷歸。

translations.literal: Zhu Mi had first sought white magpies and the like—Shengzhong would not comply; at this point he fabricated charges against him and he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mi had earlier asked for white magpies and the like, and Shengzhong had refused. Now Zhu Mi fabricated charges against him, and Shengzhong was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 建炎中，範宗尹為相，凡前日以朋附被罪遠貶者，鹹赦還，復知湖州，時群盜縱橫，聲搖諸郡，勝仲修城郭，作戰艦，閱士卒，賊知有備，引去。

translations.literal: During Jianyan, Fan Zongyin was chief minister; all who had earlier been punished for factional attachment and exiled far were pardoned and returned—Shengzhong was again made prefect of Huzhou; at the time bandits roamed freely and their fame shook the commanderies—Shengzhong repaired walls, built warships, inspected troops; the bandits knowing there was preparation withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyan era Fan Zongyin became chief minister and pardoned those earlier punished for factional ties and exiled far away. Shengzhong was again appointed prefect of Huzhou. Bandits were then rampant and threatening neighboring prefectures, but Shengzhong repaired the walls, built warships, and drilled troops. Seeing the city prepared, the bandits withdrew.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，發官廩振之，民賴以濟。

translations.literal: The year had great famine; he opened government granaries to relieve them—the people relied on this to be saved.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck he opened government granaries for relief, and the people were saved.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，丐祠歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing he requested temple office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131 he requested a temple appointment and retired home.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒，年七十三，諡文康。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died, aged seventy-three; posthumous title Wenkang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1144 at the age of seventy-three and was given the posthumous title Wenkang.

sentences.zh: 子立方，官至侍從。

translations.literal: His son Lifang reached attendance at court.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lifang rose to a position in imperial attendance.

sentences.zh: 孫邲，為右相，自有傳。

translations.literal: Sun Bin served as Right Grand Counselor; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bin served as Right Grand Counselor and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 熊克，字子復，建寧建陽人，御史大夫博之後。

translations.literal: Xiong Ke, styled Zifu, was a native of Jianyang in Jianning—a descendant of the Censor-in-Chief Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Ke, styled Zifu, came from Jianyang in Jianning and was a descendant of the Censor-in-Chief Bo.

sentences.zh: 將生，有翠羽雀翔臥內。

translations.literal: When about to be born, an emerald-feathered sparrow flew in and rested within the room.
translations.idiomatic: Just before his birth, a sparrow with emerald feathers flew into the chamber and settled there.

sentences.zh: 克幼而翹秀，既長，好學善屬文，郡博士胡憲器之，曰：“子學老於年，他日當以文章 顯。”

translations.literal: Ke from youth was outstanding; once grown, he loved learning and was skilled at composing prose. The district erudite Hu Xian esteemed him, saying: "Your learning is mature beyond your years; another day you will become eminent through literary writings."
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Ke showed exceptional talent from childhood. As an adult he loved learning and wrote well. Hu Xian, the district erudite, took notice of him and said, "You have learning beyond your years; one day you will make your name through letters."

sentences.zh: 紹興中進士第，知紹興府諸暨縣，越帥課賦頗急，諸邑率督趣以應，克曰：“寧吾獲罪，不忍困吾民。”

translations.literal: In the Shaoxing era he passed the jinshi examination, served as magistrate of Zhuji in Shaoxing Prefecture—the Yue commander-in-chief's tax levies were quite urgent, and all counties in general pressed and urged to respond. Ke said: "Better that I incur guilt than bear to distress my people."
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoxing period he passed the jinshi examination and became magistrate of Zhuji in Shaoxing Prefecture. The regional commander pressed urgently for tax collection, and every county rushed to comply. Xiong Ke said, "I would rather face punishment than squeeze my people."

sentences.zh: 他日，府遣幕僚閱視有亡，時方不雨，克對之泣 曰：“此催租時耶！”

translations.literal: Another day the prefecture sent staff officers to inspect what was missing; at the time there was drought. Ke wept before them, saying: "Is this the time to press for rent!"
translations.idiomatic: One day the prefecture sent aides to check for arrears while drought persisted. He wept before them and cried, "Is this really the moment to demand rent!"

sentences.zh: 部使者芮輝行縣至其境，謂克曰：“曩知子文墨而已，今乃見古循吏。”

translations.literal: The circuit commissioner Rui Hui toured counties and reached his jurisdiction, telling Ke: "I once knew you only for your brushwork; now I behold an ancient model magistrate."
translations.idiomatic: When circuit commissioner Rui Hui toured the county and entered his district, he told Xiong Ke, "I knew you only as a man of letters; now I see a magistrate in the old worthy mold."

sentences.zh: 為表薦之，入為提轄文思院。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial recommending him; Ke entered service as Supervisor of the Hall of Literary Reflection."
translations.idiomatic: Rui Hui recommended him by memorial, and Xiong Ke was appointed Supervisor of the Hall of Literary Reflection at court.

sentences.zh: 嘗以文獻曾覿，覿持白於 孝宗，孝宗喜之，內出御筆，除直學士院。

translations.literal: Once he presented a composition to Zeng Di; Di presented it to Emperor Xiaozong, who was pleased with it. The emperor issued an inner draft in his own hand and appointed him directly to the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted a piece of writing to Zeng Di, who showed it to Emperor Xiaozong. The emperor was delighted and issued a personal edict appointing Xiong Ke directly to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 宰相趙雄甚異之，因奏曰：“翰院清選，熊克小臣，不由論薦而得，無以服眾論，請自朝廷召試，然後用之。”

translations.literal: Grand Counselor Zhao Xiong was greatly struck by this and memorialized: "The Hanlin Institute is a pure selection; Xiong Ke is a minor official who obtained appointment without deliberation and recommendation—there is no way to satisfy public opinion. I request that the court summon him for examination and then employ him."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Counselor Zhao Xiong was greatly surprised and memorialized, "The Hanlin Academy is an elite appointment. Xiong Ke is a minor official who received it without the usual review and recommendation, and that will not satisfy critics. Let the court summon him for examination before appointing him."

sentences.zh: 上曰：“ 善。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Very well."

sentences.zh: 乃以為校書郎，累遷學士院權直，上御選德殿，召諭曰：“卿製誥甚工，且有體，自此燕閑可論治道。”

translations.literal: He was then made Collator, and through successive promotions became Acting Hanlin Academician. The emperor attended at the Hall of Virtuous Selection, summoned him and instructed: "Your drafting of edicts is very skilled and has proper form; from now on in leisure moments you may discuss the way of governance."
translations.idiomatic: He was made Collator and eventually rose to Acting Hanlin Academician. The emperor received him at the Hall of Virtuous Selection and said, "You draft edicts with great skill and proper style. When we have leisure, you may discuss statecraft with me."

sentences.zh: 克自以見知於上，數有論奏。

translations.literal: Ke, considering himself recognized by the emperor, repeatedly submitted policy memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling he had won the emperor's trust, Xiong Ke submitted policy proposals again and again.

sentences.zh: 嚐言：“ 金人雖講和，而不能保於他日，今宜以和為守，以守為攻。

translations.literal: He once said: "Although the Jurchen have made peace, they cannot be guaranteed on another day; now one ought to take peace as defense and defense as attack."
translations.idiomatic: He once argued, "Though the Jurchen are at peace with us, that peace may not hold. For now we should treat peace as a form of defense, and defense as preparation for attack.

sentences.zh: 當和好之時，為備守之計，彼不能禁吾不為也。

translations.literal: At the time of friendly relations, make plans for defense and preparedness—they cannot forbid us from not doing so.
translations.idiomatic: While relations remain amicable, we should prepare our defenses; they cannot stop us from doing so.

sentences.zh: 邊備既實，金人萬一猖獗，必不得誌於我，退而乘我，曲 不在我矣。

translations.literal: Once border preparations are solid, if the Jurchen by chance run wild, they will certainly not achieve their aim against us; if they withdraw and then strike us, the fault will not lie with us.
translations.idiomatic: Once our frontier defenses are strong, even if the Jurchen grow aggressive they cannot prevail against us. If they retreat and then turn on us, the moral blame will not be ours.

sentences.zh: 且今日之守，莫重淮東。

translations.literal: Moreover, of today's defenses none is heavier than east of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Of all our defensive priorities today, none matters more than the eastern Huai region.

sentences.zh: 金犯淮西，負糧自隨，其勢必難。

translations.literal: If the Jin invade west of the Huai, bearing grain with them, their situation will inevitably be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: A Jin attack across the western Huai would force them to carry their own supplies, making the campaign far harder.

sentences.zh: 若犯淮東，清河糧船直下，易耳。

translations.literal: If they invade east of the Huai, grain boats on the Clear River descend straight down—it is easy.
translations.idiomatic: An attack east of the Huai would let grain ships sail straight down the Qing River, making supply much easier.

sentences.zh: 然則守淮之策，以墾田、修堰、教民兵為先。

translations.literal: Thus the strategy for defending the Huai: take opening farmland, repairing dams, and training militia as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: The strategy for holding the Huai should prioritize land reclamation, dyke repair, and militia training.

sentences.zh: 援淮東之策， 莫若即江陰建水軍，緩急可相應。

translations.literal: The strategy for reinforcing east of the Huai—none is better than establishing a naval force at Jiangyin, so that in urgency or ease they may respond to each other.
translations.idiomatic: The best way to support the eastern Huai is to establish a naval force at Jiangyin that can respond quickly in crisis.

sentences.zh: 然驟立一軍，慮敵生疑，當托以海道商賈之衝，多奪攘，置一巡檢警督之，自此歲增兵，不出十年，隱然一軍矣。

translations.literal: Yet to suddenly establish an army would fear arousing enemy suspicion; one should use as pretext the sea route's merchant traffic being a chokepoint with much plunder—establish one inspector to warn and supervise; from then yearly increase troops; within ten years, covertly there will be an army.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden new army would alarm the enemy. Better to cite the rampant piracy on the sea lanes, post an inspector to patrol the route, and increase troops year by year. Within ten years we would quietly have a full force.

sentences.zh: 中興之際，不患 兵不可用，而患將權難收。

translations.literal: In the Restoration period, there was no worry that troops could not be used, but worry that command authority was hard to consolidate.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of the Restoration, the concern was not that soldiers could not fight, but that military authority was hard to bring back under central control.

sentences.zh: 今日之弊，不患將不可馭，而患軍情易動。

translations.literal: Today's flaw: there is no worry that commanders cannot be controlled, but worry that army morale is easy to stir.
translations.idiomatic: Today's problem is no longer unmanageable generals but troops whose temper is easily unsettled.

sentences.zh: 往時諸大將拊士卒如家人，自罷諸將兵權，御前主帥，更徙不常，凡軍中筦榷之利，所以養士 卒者，今皆轉而為包苴矣，又朘其餘以佐之，得無怨乎！

translations.literal: Formerly the great commanders treated soldiers as family; since the dismissal of the great commanders' military authority, Imperial Front commanders, transferred and changed constantly—every profit from monopoly in the army used to nurture soldiers, now all turned into bribes; moreover they cut the remainder to supplement them—is there no resentment!
translations.idiomatic: In the past great generals treated their men like family. Since those generals were stripped of command and Imperial Front commanders were rotated endlessly, the monopolies that once supported the troops have become bribes instead, with whatever is left skimmed away on top—how could soldiers not resent it!

sentences.zh: 宜嚴戒將帥，毋縱掊削。”

translations.literal: One ought strictly to warn commanders, not to allow extortion and squeezing."
translations.idiomatic: Commanders should be sternly warned not to exploit their men."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其有誌，召草明堂赦書。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him for having resolve and summoned him to draft the Hall of Brightness amnesty edict."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his public-spiritedness and had him draft the amnesty edict for the Hall of Brightness rites.

sentences.zh: 克言：“二浙薦饑，蝗且起，赦文不宜飾詞。”

translations.literal: Ke said: "The two Zhe regions face impending famine, locusts are about to rise—the amnesty text ought not employ ornate words."
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Ke said, "The two Zhe provinces face famine and locusts are rising; the amnesty proclamation should not use flowery language."

sentences.zh: 帝 嘉其識體。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his grasp of propriety."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his sense of what was appropriate.

sentences.zh: 除起居郎兼直學士院，以言者出知台州，奉祠。

translations.literal: He was appointed Recorder and concurrent Hanlin Academician; because of critics he was sent out as prefect of Taizhou, then granted a stipend shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Recorder and Hanlin Academician, but critics drove him out to serve as prefect of Taizhou before he received a stipend appointment.

sentences.zh: 克博聞強記，自少至老，著述外無他嗜。

translations.literal: Ke had broad learning and strong memory; from youth to old age, apart from writing he had no other obsessions.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Ke was widely learned with a prodigious memory, and from youth to old age wrote almost to the exclusion of all else.

sentences.zh: 尤淹習宋朝典故，有問者酬對如響。

translations.literal: He especially steeped himself in Song dynasty precedents and institutions; when questioned he answered as if in echo.
translations.idiomatic: He knew Song institutional history inside out and answered every question on the spot as though the reply were already waiting.

sentences.zh: 家素儉約，雖貴不改，舊所居卑陋，門不容轍，雖部使者、郡守至，必降車乃入。

translations.literal: His household was by nature frugal; though honored he did not change. His old residence was low and shabby—the gate could not accommodate a carriage wheel; though circuit commissioners and prefects came, they had to alight from the carriage before entering.
translations.idiomatic: He came from a frugal family and did not change when he rose to high office. His old home was so narrow the gate would not admit a carriage, and even visiting commissioners and prefects had to dismount before entering.

sentences.zh: 嚐愛臨川童子王克勤之才，將妻以女而乏資遣，會草制獲賜金，遂以歸之，人稱其清介。

translations.literal: He once admired the talent of the Linchuan youth Wang Keqin, planning to marry his daughter to him but lacking dowry funds; it happened he received bestowed gold while drafting an edict, and so gave it for her marriage—people praised his integrity and aloofness.
translations.idiomatic: He admired the young scholar Wang Keqin of Linchuan and wished to marry his daughter to him but lacked a dowry. When he received a gold grant for drafting an edict, he gave it for the marriage, and people praised his incorruptible character.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 張即之

translations.literal: Zhang Jizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jizhi

sentences.zh: 張即之，字溫夫，參知政事孝伯之子。

translations.literal: Zhang Jizhi, styled Wenfu, was the son of Vice Grand Counselor Xiaobo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jizhi, styled Wenfu, was the son of Vice Grand Counselor Zhang Xiaobo.

sentences.zh: 以父恩授承務郎，銓中兩浙轉運司進士舉，曆監平江府糧料院。

translations.literal: By his father's grace he was granted Master of Service; he passed selection in the Two-Zhe Transport Commission jinshi quota, and served as superintendent of the Pingjiang Prefecture grain office.
translations.idiomatic: By privilege of his father's rank he received the office of Master of Service, passed the jinshi quota of the Two-Zhe Transport Commission, and served as superintendent of the Pingjiang Prefecture grain office.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，監臨安府樓店務。

translations.literal: Upon his father's mourning, when the mourning period ended, he served as superintendent of the Lin'an Prefecture inn office.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father's death, he was appointed superintendent of the Lin'an Prefecture inn office.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，監臨安府 龍山稅、寧國府城下酒曲務，簽書荊門軍判官廳公事，烏程丞，特差簽書江陰軍判官廳公事，提領戶部犒賞酒庫所幹辦公事，添差兩浙轉運司主管文字，行在檢點贍 軍激賞酒庫所主管文字，監尚書六部門，淮南東路提舉常平司主管文字，添差通判揚州，改鎮江，又改嘉興，將作監簿，軍器監丞，司農寺丞，知嘉興，未赴，以言 者罷，丐祠，主管雲台觀，引年告老，特授直秘閣致仕。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's mourning, when the mourning period ended, he served as superintendent of the Longshan tax office in Lin'an Prefecture and superintendent of the lower-city wine monopoly office in Ningguo Prefecture; signing secretary for general affairs at the Jingmen military judge's office; assistant magistrate of Wucheng; specially assigned signing secretary for general affairs at the Jiangyin military judge's office; manager of general affairs at the Ministry of Revenue Commemorative Wine Warehouse; additionally assigned document controller at the Two-Zhe Transport Commission; document controller at the temporary capital's inspection office for army-support and reward wine warehouses; superintendent of the Six Ministries gate; document controller at the Huainan East Circuit Ever-Normal Granary Office; additionally assigned as vice prefect of Yangzhou, transferred to Zhenjiang, then again to Jiaxing; registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings; assistant director of the Directorate of Armaments; assistant director of the Ministry of Revenue; prefect of Jiaxing—before he took up the post, critics had him dismissed; he requested a stipend shrine; served as director of the Cloud Terrace Abbey; citing age he petitioned to retire and was specially granted Directly Assembled Secretariat Pavilion and retirement.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother, he served in succession as superintendent of the Longshan tax office in Lin'an Prefecture and superintendent of the lower-city wine monopoly office in Ningguo Prefecture; signing secretary for general affairs at the Jingmen military judge's office; assistant magistrate of Wucheng; specially assigned signing secretary for general affairs at the Jiangyin military judge's office; manager of general affairs at the Ministry of Revenue Commemorative Wine Warehouse; additionally assigned document controller at the Two-Zhe Transport Commission; document controller at the temporary capital's inspection office for army-support and reward wine warehouses; superintendent of the Six Ministries gate; document controller at the Huainan East Circuit Ever-Normal Granary Office; additionally assigned as vice prefect of Yangzhou, then transferred to Zhenjiang and again to Jiaxing; registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings; assistant director of the Directorate of Armaments; assistant director of the Ministry of Revenue; and prefect of Jiaxing. Before he could take up the prefecture, critics had him removed. He petitioned for a stipend shrine, served as director of the Cloud Terrace Abbey, and citing age petitioned to retire, receiving the special grant of Directly Assembled Secretariat Pavilion and retirement.

sentences.zh: 寶祐四年，制置使余晦入蜀，以讒劾閬州守王惟忠。

translations.literal: In Baoyou year 4, when Pacification Commissioner Yu Hui entered Shu, he slanderously impeached Wang Weizhong, prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoyou year 4, when Pacification Commissioner Yu Hui entered Shu, he slanderously impeached Wang Weizhong, prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是削惟忠五官，沒入其資，下詔獄，鍛煉誣伏，坐棄市。

translations.literal: Thereupon Weizhong was stripped of five offices, his property was confiscated, he was sent to the imperial prison, and through coerced fabrication was falsely made to confess and sentenced to execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Weizhong was stripped of five offices, his property was confiscated, he was sent to the imperial prison, and through coerced fabrication was falsely made to confess and sentenced to execution in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 惟忠臨刑，謂其友陳大方曰：「吾死當上愬於天。」

translations.literal: When Weizhong faced execution, he said to his friend Chen Dafang, “When I die, I shall appeal upward to Heaven.”
translations.idiomatic: When Weizhong faced execution, he said to his friend Chen Dafang, “When I die, I shall appeal upward to Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 七揮刃不殊，血逆流。

translations.literal: Seven times the blade was swung but did not sever him, and the blood flowed backward.
translations.idiomatic: Seven times the blade was swung but did not sever him, and the blood flowed backward.

sentences.zh: 即之雖閒居，移書言於淮東制置使賈似道恤其遺孤。

translations.literal: Although Jizhi was living in retirement, he sent a letter to Huai East Pacification Commissioner Jia Sidao asking him to care for Weizhong’s surviving orphan.
translations.idiomatic: Although Jizhi was living in retirement, he sent a letter to Huai East Pacification Commissioner Jia Sidao asking him to care for Weizhong’s surviving orphan.

sentences.zh: 又使從孫士倩娶惟忠孤女。

translations.literal: He also had his collateral grandson Shiqian marry Weizhong’s orphaned daughter.
translations.idiomatic: He also had his collateral grandson Shiqian marry Weizhong’s orphaned daughter.

sentences.zh: 未幾，似道入相，中書舍人常挺亦以為言。

translations.literal: Before long, Sidao entered the chancellery, and Secretariat Drafter Chang Ting also spoke on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Sidao entered the chancellery, and Secretariat Drafter Chang Ting also spoke on the matter.

sentences.zh: 景定元年，給還首領，以禮改葬，復金壇田，多即之倡義云。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingding, Weizhong’s head was returned, he was reburied with proper rites, and his fields at Jintan were restored; much of this is said to have been initiated by Jizhi’s sense of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingding, Weizhong’s head was returned, he was reburied with proper rites, and his fields at Jintan were restored; much of this is said to have been initiated by Jizhi’s sense of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 即之以能書聞天下，金人尤寶其翰墨。

translations.literal: Jizhi was known throughout the realm for his calligraphy, and the Jin people especially treasured his brushwork.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi was known throughout the realm for his calligraphy, and the Jin people especially treasured his brushwork.

sentences.zh: 惟忠字肖尊，慶元之鄞人，嘉定十三年進士。

translations.literal: Weizhong, styled Xiaozun, was a native of Yin in Qingyuan; passed the jinshi examination in the thirteenth year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong, styled Xiaozun, came from Yin in Qingyuan and passed the jinshi examination in 1220.

sentences.zh: 附 趙蕃

translations.literal: Appended: Zhao Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fan (appended biography)

sentences.zh: 趙蕃字昌父，其先鄭州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Fan, styled Changfu—his ancestors were natives of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fan, styled Changfu, came from a family originally of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，大父暘以秘書少監出提點坑冶，寓信州之玉山。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan, his grandfather Yang went out as Vice Director of the Secretariat as Commissioner of Mining and Smelting, and lodged at Yushan in Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyan era his grandfather Yang left the capital as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Commissioner of Mining and Smelting, settling at Yushan in Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 蕃以暘致仕恩，補州文學。

translations.literal: Fan, by Yang's retired grace, filled the post of Prefecture Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fan received the post of prefectural erudite through his grandfather Yang's retirement privilege.

sentences.zh: 調浮梁尉、連江主簿，皆不赴。

translations.literal: He was assigned as magistrate of Fuliang and chief clerk of Lianjiang—both he did not take up.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered posts as magistrate of Fuliang and chief clerk of Lianjiang but declined both.

sentences.zh: 為太和主簿，受知於楊萬里。

translations.literal: He served as chief clerk of Taihe and received recognition from Yang Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: As chief clerk of Taihe he won the admiration of Yang Wanli.

sentences.zh: 調辰州司理參軍，與郡守爭獄，罷，人以蕃為直。

translations.literal: Assigned as judicial adjutant of Chenzhou, he contended over a case with the prefect and was dismissed; people regarded Fan as upright.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as judicial officer of Chenzhou, he disputed a case with the prefect and was removed from office; people regarded Zhao Fan as a man of integrity.

sentences.zh: 始，蕃受學於劉清之，清之守衡州，乃求監安仁贍軍酒庫，因以卒業。

translations.literal: At first Fan studied under Liu Qingzhi; when Qingzhi was prefect of Hengzhou, he therefore sought to serve as superintendent of the Anren army-support wine warehouse, thereby completing his studies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fan first studied with Liu Qingzhi. When Qingzhi became prefect of Hengzhou, Fan asked to serve as superintendent of the Anren army-support wine warehouse so he could finish his studies nearby.

sentences.zh: 至衡而清之罷，蕃即丐祠，從清之歸。

translations.literal: When he reached Hengzhou, Qingzhi was dismissed; Fan immediately petitioned for a stipend shrine and returned with Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived at Hengzhou, Qingzhi had already lost his post. Zhao Fan immediately petitioned for a stipend appointment and went home with his teacher.

sentences.zh: 其後真德秀書之《國史》曰：“蕃於師友之際蓋如 此，肯負國乎！”

translations.literal: Later Zhen Dexiu wrote in the National History, "Zhao Fan was this devoted to his teachers and friends—how could he betray his country!"
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhen Dexiu wrote in the National History, "Zhao Fan was this devoted to his teachers and friends—how could he betray his country!"

sentences.zh: 家居，連書祠官之考者三十有一，理宗即位，以太社令與劉宰同召，不拜，特改奉議郎、直秘閣，又辭。

translations.literal: Living at home, he continuously submitted thirty-one annual evaluations for stipend posts; when Emperor Lizong acceded, together with Liu Zai he was summoned as Grand Sacrificer for Earth—he did not accept; he was specially changed to Proposal-Discussing Gentleman and Directly Assembled Secretariat Pavilion, and again declined."
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement and submitted thirty-one consecutive annual review reports for his stipend post. When Emperor Lizong came to the throne, he and Liu Zai were summoned to serve as Grand Sacrificer of Earth. He refused, was specially granted the rank of Proposal-Discussing Gentleman and Directly Assembled Secretariat Pavilion, and declined again.

sentences.zh: 奉祠，得致仕，轉承議郎，依前直秘閣。

translations.literal: He held a stipend shrine, obtained retirement, was promoted to Order-Discussing Gentleman, continuing as before Directly Assembled Secretariat Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He retained his stipend appointment, received formal retirement, was promoted to Order-Discussing Gentleman, and kept his Directly Assembled Secretariat Pavilion title.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十七。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 蕃年五十，猶問學於朱熹。

translations.literal: Fan at age fifty still inquired and studied under Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Even at fifty Zhao Fan continued his studies with Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 既耄，猶患末路之難，命所居曰難齋。

translations.literal: Once aged, he still worried over the difficulty of the final path, naming his residence Difficulty Studio.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he still worried about life's final trials and named his study the Studio of Difficulty.

sentences.zh: 蕃賦性寬平，與人樂易而剛介不可奪。

translations.literal: Fan's innate disposition was mild and even; with others he was easy and pleasant, yet firm and uncompromising—nothing could wrest it away.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Zhao Fan was open and even-tempered, easy in company, yet resolute and unyielding in matters of principle.

sentences.zh: 丞相周必大與蕃契，屢加引 薦，蕃竟不受。

translations.literal: Grand Counselor Zhou Bida was close with Fan and repeatedly recommended him; Fan in the end did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Counselor Zhou Bida was fond of him and recommended him many times, but Zhao Fan always refused.

sentences.zh: 宰之言曰：“文獻之家，典刑之彥，巋然獨存，猶有以係學者之望者，蕃一人而已。”

translations.literal: Zai said: "Families of literary virtue, exemplary figures of law and precedent—solely remaining steadfast, there is still one to bind scholars' hopes: Fan alone."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zai said, "In a house of literary distinction, among the last exemplars of the old standard still standing, one man alone keeps scholars' hopes alive — and that is Zhao Fan."

sentences.zh: 信州守吳旂乞錄其後，詔其子遂補上州文學，遂亦力辭。

translations.literal: The Xinzhou prefect Wu Qi petitioned to record his posterity; an edict ordered his son Sui to fill Upper Prefecture Erudite; Sui also forcefully declined."
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Xinzhou, Wu Qi, asked that his descendants be granted office. The emperor ordered his son Zhao Sui to receive the post of upper-prefecture erudite, but Sui firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 又詔 以承務郎致仕，與一子恩澤。

translations.literal: Again an edict granted retirement as Master of Service, with one son's grace privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict granted him retirement at the rank of Master of Service and one privilege appointment for a son.

sentences.zh: 景定三年，秘閣修撰鄭協等請諡，乃諡文節。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingding, Secretariat Pavilion Compiler Zheng Xie and others requested a posthumous title; he was posthumously titled Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: In 1262 compilers of the Secretariat Pavilion including Zheng Xie petitioned for a posthumous title, and he was given the posthumous name Wenjie.
